about: Every generated image in Blackwood Investigations. Run: node scripts/generate-art.mjs (see art/README.md). Prompts are built as style + kind + subject. Characters reuse the same description everywhere so they look like the same person. Walkable rooms (wall, floor, ceiling, trim, piece, fixture, outside, model, turn) use the case's flat look line from looks instead of its lit style; their room records are in rooms. See art/WALKABLE.md.
style: Painted noir illustration in the manner of a 1980s paperback mystery cover and classic hand-painted point-and-click adventure game backgrounds. Gouache and oil textures with visible brushwork, warm tungsten lamplight against deep blue-black shadows, a muted palette of ochre, oxblood, bottle green, slate and nicotine cream, subtle film grain. Los Angeles, August 1985. Period-accurate details. The only readable words are the ones the subject spells out, printed exactly as written and correctly spelled; all other paperwork shows soft, unreadable typing or handwriting. No logos, brand names, watermarks or signatures.

background.suffix: A wide establishing interior view at standing eye level, composed for a 16:9 game screen, with depth and atmosphere. The room is empty of people. Keep the described empty surfaces and floor areas genuinely clear, because objects and people will be placed there separately.

portrait.suffix: A painted head-and-shoulders portrait facing the viewer directly, looking straight into the camera, head centered and level, mouth gently closed, nothing covering the mouth or eyes, even soft light from the front, against a dark, muted painted backdrop. Natural, believable face; not a caricature.

figure.suffix: The same person as the reference portrait, shown full length from head to toe, standing naturally, turned three-quarters toward the viewer, lit warmly from the upper left. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background: no floor, no ground, no backdrop, no shadow and no painted patch beneath the feet; nothing in the image except the person. The whole person fits inside the frame, with empty space above the head and below the shoes: both feet and shoes fully visible, never cropped at the ankles, shins or knees.

sprite.suffix: A single isolated object, centered, entirely in frame, seen at a three-quarter angle from slightly above as it would sit in a room, lit warmly from the upper left to match a painted scene. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background: no surface, no shadow and no painted patch beneath it; nothing in the image except the object.

evidence.suffix: A close-up evidence still life, raking lamplight, shallow depth of field, dark muted surroundings, the subject filling most of the frame.

site.suffix: A cinematic wide composition with room on the left third for page text, moody and atmospheric.

panorama.suffix: A wide side-on panorama, as seen through the side window of a moving car, composed for a 16:9 screen. The horizon runs level across the whole image and nothing important touches the left or right edge, so the image can repeat side by side. The bottom fifth is plain dark ground.

strip.suffix: Seen exactly side-on, lit by warm dusk and streetlight. Output a PNG with a truly transparent background (a real alpha channel, not a painted checkerboard pattern): nothing in the image except the subject.

pov.suffix: A cinematic first-person view at standing eye level, composed for a 16:9 screen, the way ahead leading into the picture. No people.

map.suffix: A hand-painted fold-out street map from the 1980s, seen flat from directly above and filling the whole image edge to edge like a sheet laid on a table: no table, no border, no frame. Muted period map colours: cream paper, ochre streets, sage green parkland, pale blue water, faint fold creases. Absolutely no words, letters, numbers, street names or symbols anywhere on the map.

face.suffix: An edit of the reference portrait: the same painting of the same person, at the same size, framing, pose, lighting, colors and brushwork. Change nothing except what the subject asks for. Do not move the head, change the expression elsewhere, or redraw the hair, clothing or background. Return one single image, never a sheet of several faces.

wall.suffix: A seamless, tileable texture of a plain interior wall surface, seen perfectly straight on and level, filling the whole image edge to edge. It must tile: the left edge continues exactly into the right edge and the top into the bottom, with no seams, borders or vignetting, and an even pattern and color across the whole image. Only the surface itself: no doors, windows, pictures, switches, outlets, furniture, baseboards, chair rails, crown molding, corners, ceiling or floor. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

floor.suffix: A seamless, tileable texture looking straight down at a floor or the ground, filling the whole image edge to edge. It must tile: the left edge continues exactly into the right edge and the top into the bottom, with no seams, borders or vignetting, and even wear and color across the whole image. Only the surface: no furniture, rugs, objects, walls or baseboards. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

ceiling.suffix: A seamless, tileable texture looking straight up at a ceiling, filling the whole image edge to edge. It must tile: the left edge continues exactly into the right edge and the top into the bottom, with no seams, borders or vignetting. Only the surface: no light fixtures, fans, vents, walls, corners or crown molding. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

trim.suffix: A straight length of interior trim molding seen perfectly straight on and level, the molding's face filling the whole image from the top edge to the bottom edge and running off both the left and right edges. It must tile from left to right: the left edge continues exactly into the right edge, with no ends, joints, corners or nail holes. No wall, floor or ceiling visible above or below it. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

piece.suffix: One flat thing that hangs on or is set into an interior wall, seen perfectly straight on and level, as if photographed square to the wall, filling most of the frame with a little empty space around it. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background: no wall around it, no floor, no shadow. Any glass (window panes, a door's window, an empty frame) and any open gap is completely transparent: empty, with no glass, reflection or view drawn in it. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

fixture.suffix: A ceiling light fixture seen from directly below, looking straight up at it, centered and entirely in frame. Switched off: no glow, no light. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background: no ceiling around it, no shadow. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

outside.suffix: The view seen through a window or open doorway, at standing eye level about 5 and a half feet, composed so any part of it can be shown. Just the view: no window frame, curtains, glass, wall or door. The level horizon runs straight across; nothing important is cut by the edges.

model.suffix: A reference picture for making a 3D model: one single object, standing upright in its normal position, seen from the front and slightly to one side and slightly above, entirely in frame and centered. Isolated cut-out on a fully transparent background: no floor, no shadow, nothing else in the image. Clear, true colors and materials. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

turn.suffix: The same person as the reference portrait, shown full length for making a 3D character: standing upright and straight, feet slightly apart, arms hanging relaxed a little away from the sides, the whole figure in frame from the top of the head to the soles of the shoes. Plain light gray background. Soft, even, flat light from every direction: no cast shadows, no light patches, no lamps switched on, no glow, no sunlight.

images.subject: Night view across a private investigator's desk in 1985 Los Angeles: venetian blinds throw stripes of streetlight over a fedora, a manila case folder and a glass of whiskey; beyond the window, city lights and palm-tree silhouettes against a deep blue sky.

A 1920s Spanish-revival house on a quiet Los Feliz street at night under a purple jacaranda tree, a single lamp lit in one window, a large dark sedan parked at the curb with its lights off, a streetlight casting a pool of amber light.

A private investigator's office on the eleventh floor of an older Wilshire Boulevard building at night, seen from a standing position just in front of a large dark wooden desk, looking slightly down onto it. The desk is close to the viewer and runs the full width of the lower part of the frame; its wide, flat top is clearly visible as a broad surface filling the bottom third of the image, completely clear and empty except a green banker's lamp at the far right end. Beyond the desk, an empty leather desk chair, and behind it a tall window with venetian blinds and city lights. On the left wall, a cork board with pinned papers, photographs and red string, above a filing cabinet. On the right wall, a large framed street map. At the far right, a small side table holding a black manual typewriter, and a coat stand with a trench coat and fedora. No people.

The living room of a widow's 1920s Spanish-revival house in Los Feliz, the quiet morning after a crime. Against the left wall, a roll-top writing desk with its top clear and one filing drawer pulled partly open. Left of center on the back wall, a solid oak front door. In the middle of the back wall, an arched doorway leading to a kitchen. On the right, a mahogany sideboard with a glass cake stand, stacked dessert plates and a two-thirds empty wine bottle. At the far right, a brick fireplace with a stand of fireplace tools. A chintz sofa on the left side of the floor. A patterned rug with a large open, clear area of floor in the center foreground. Faint police tape outlines on the carpet. No people.

The small, tidy kitchen of the same 1920s house, morning light. At center back, a window above a white enamel sink, the window open a few inches behind an aluminium insect screen. At the right, a wooden back door with a small window and a brass bolt. On the left wall, a pharmacy wall calendar and a beige wall telephone with a long coiled cord. Tiled counters with clear empty counter space to the left of the sink and beside it. At the far left edge, a doorway back to the living room.

A 24-hour diner on Sunset Boulevard at night in 1985. At the left, a red vinyl window booth with the night street and a pay phone visible outside. A long counter with chrome stools runs across the middle; behind the counter in the center is open, clear space where a waitress will stand. On the counter, a glass pie display case. At the right end of the counter, a cash register with clear counter space beside it. On the back wall near the kitchen pass, a pinned paper staff schedule. At the far right, a chrome 1950s jukebox. Warm neon glow.

A tidy bachelor apartment on the second floor of a Silver Lake building in 1985. At the left near the entry door, a clear empty stretch of wall and floor where a coat rack will stand. On the right, a modern desk with neat stacks of labelled client folders and a clear patch of desktop. A low coffee table in the center foreground with a clear top. Beige walls, venetian blinds, a framed abstract print, a kitchenette counter with clear space at the far right. A clear open area of floor in the center for a person to stand.

The front room of a retired schoolteacher's modest 1950s bungalow. At the left, a large front window with lace curtains looking across the street at a Spanish-revival house, a purple jacaranda tree and a streetlight. At the right, a wood console television set with rabbit-ear antennas, a reading armchair, bookshelves, and a clear patch of wall above the television for a framed photograph. A braided rug with clear open floor in the center for a person to stand and a clear spot near the front for a cat.

An independent auto repair garage in Atwater Village in 1985, daytime. Center right, an old pickup truck raised on a hydraulic lift with a drop light hanging under it. Along the left wall, a long tool bench with tools in labelled trays, a coffee can of bolts and a radio. On the right wall, a board of carbon-copy work orders on nails. Concrete floor with oil stains, an open roll-up bay door with daylight. A clear open area of floor at left of center for a mechanic to stand.

The loan department of a 1985 savings and loan office on Vermont Avenue, daytime. On the left wall, a row of steel four-drawer filing cabinets. A wooden desk at center right with a clear empty desktop, and a chair behind it with clear space for a person to stand. On the right wall, a cork notice board with rate sheets. Large windows with venetian blinds and daylight, beige and brown corporate decor, a potted plant.
A gentle portrait, as if from a framed photograph on a mantel.
In her front room, lamplight.
In his apartment, the window blinds behind him.
In his garage, a work light behind him.
At her office, daylight through blinds.
At a squad-room desk, holding a telephone receiver near his ear.

Wiping his hands on the red shop rag.
Holding a manila folder against her chest.
Holding a glass coffee pot.

A thin pale blue laboratory report folder lying flat.

A man's right hand held at his side, the palm and heel wrapped in a fresh, clean white gauze bandage, the cuff of a pale blue shirt and a gold wristwatch visible.
The left half of a typed bank statement torn from top to bottom, several lines circled in pencil and a short pencilled note in the margin; all text blurred and illegible.

Los Angeles at dusk in 1985, seen side-on from a boulevard: a long line of low hills with scattered house lights, the downtown towers small on the far horizon, a deep violet to amber sky with a few long clouds, and rows of low commercial buildings and apartment blocks in near-silhouette with warm lit windows. No cars, no people, no signs with lettering.

A long row of roadside silhouettes beside a Los Angeles boulevard: tall palm trees of different heights, two curved 1960s streetlights with warm glowing lamps, a low stucco wall and a few shrubs. Everything stands on one level baseline along the very bottom edge of the image, evenly spaced across the full width so the row can repeat. No sky, no road, no buildings.

A 1979 four-door American sedan in faded brown with chrome trim, seen exactly side-on in profile and facing right, headlights on and a warm glow from the dashboard, the silhouette of a man in a fedora at the wheel. Whole car in frame with space around it; only a faint contact shadow under the tyres.

Crossing Hollister Avenue in Los Feliz at night, looking straight across the quiet street: a row of 1920s Spanish-revival houses with red tile roofs and warm lit windows, a jacaranda tree in purple blossom under an amber streetlight, a few 1970s and 80s sedans parked along the curb, palm silhouettes against a deep blue sky, the asphalt and painted crosswalk leading toward the far curb.

Northeast Los Angeles in 1985. Across the top quarter, the green wooded hills of Griffith Park with a few winding park roads. The Los Angeles River, a pale blue channel with concrete banks, enters at the top just right of centre and curves down through the right third to the bottom right corner. A broad boulevard crosses the lower third from left to right. Everywhere else a dense grid of streets with small blocks of houses and tiny palm trees, a few larger avenues running north to south, and a small cluster of downtown towers drawn in the bottom right corner beside the river.

A quiet residential street in a small California coastal town at 3:40 in the morning, low fog drifting under palm trees. On the right, a small 1950s stucco house with a one-car garage, every window dark. At the curb in front of it, a dark full-size van with no windows down its side is pulling away with its headlights off, a faint wisp of exhaust in the cold air. Across the street, a single lit window where an old man's silhouette watches from behind the curtain. A streetlight at the far corner throws a pool of amber light onto the wet asphalt the van is about to pass through. The left third of the image is quiet dark fog and sky.

A dark radio station office high above Chicago on a rainy night in 1927. Through a tall window, Art Deco towers lit amber, the elevated train on its trestle, Model T cars on the wet street and a lit bridge over the river under a cloudy moon. Inside, on a polished desk, a gray fedora, a glass of whiskey, an ashtray, a pen on typed pages, a brass carbon microphone on its stand, a radio receiver with three glowing dials, headphones and a record turntable; a wall clock and a red ON AIR lamp glowing behind glass. The left third is the window and the city.

Chicago in 1927, painted like a period street map. Lake Michigan in deep blue along the whole right edge. The Chicago River coming in from the lake just above center, then running west and splitting into north and south branches in a Y. South of the main river by the lake, the dense Loop with tiny Art Deco towers and the elevated train in a ring. North of the river, the Near North Side. Along the far left a long street running north to south. In the bottom right corner, a leafy neighborhood by the lake with a park. A street grid everywhere else, rail yards in the lower middle.

Four black-and-white police photographs and a pencil floor sketch of a radio studio, fanned out on a desk: a man face down on a carpet, a microphone stand on its side, a drawn curtain, a split door bracket.
A typed coroner's report on letterhead, several pages clipped together, under a desk lamp.

A split black cast-iron door bar bracket hanging by its two long screws from a heavy oak studio door frame, a pale splintered gouge in the wood behind it, and beside it, low in the wall at floor level, a square wooden access panel about two feet across painted the color of the wall, with no handle or fastening on this side. In raking light.
A typed radio program schedule for an evening, pinned to a wall with thumbtacks.
A buff index card with typed lines struck through in ink and handwriting below, with a small handwritten note clipped to it.
A twelve-inch aluminum recording disc half out of a paper sleeve, the sleeve labeled in pencil exactly 'A-114'.
A long stenographer's transcript in typed lines on onionskin paper, stapled, with a pencil note at the bottom.
A ruled ledger open on a workbench beside a disc-cutting lathe, columns of handwritten entries.
A long strip of paper with four inked pen traces, unrolled from a clockwork recorder drum.
Three handwritten letters on personal stationery tied in a bundle with a rubber band.
An open rooming-house register with handwritten entries, a pen in the gutter.
A handwritten letter on radio station notepaper, folded in thirds, beside its slit envelope.
A green cloth ledger open to columns of figures with small pencil tick marks in the margin.
Two typed invoices pinned together, one a carbon copy, on a secretary's desk.
A printed delivery receipt tacked to a wooden crate stenciled exactly 'RADIO CABINETS', bottles of whiskey in straw showing under the lid.
A black leather desk diary open on a blotter, one line struck through twice.
A handwritten signed statement on office notepaper, neat secretarial handwriting.
A heavy round brass weight from a microphone floor stand, wiped bright in streaks, a dark crust in its center thread, beside a balled-up stained gray rag.
A police chemist's typed report on letterhead, with a glass slide and a small evidence envelope beside it.
A ruled equipment register book open on a shelf, a pencil note at the bottom of the page.
A two-page letter in green ink on lavender notepaper.
A typed police summary, several pages, with a detective's pencil notes in the margins.
A small sheet torn from a pocket memorandum book, pencil writing, stuck on a desk spike among other papers.
A thick green cloth ledger with no title, open to handwritten columns of dates, cases and dollar figures.
A quick pencil sketch of a warehouse plan on the back of a tally sheet.
Five manila shipping tags with string, written on in cramped pencil handwriting, beside a carpenter's pencil stub.
A black Packard sedan with a chauffeur at the wheel stopped under a lamp by a watchman's shed at night, a tall man in a gray overcoat and white scarf getting out of the back.
A single sheet of ruled accounting paper, folded in four and opened, columns of figures in a firm slanted hand.

The same man as the reference portrait, same pose, light and backdrop, now with a fresh cut on his scalp above the left ear: a short dark scab and a little bruising at the hairline, partly hidden under a faded navy ball cap pushed back on his head. Nothing else changes.
Two loops of black plastic cable tie, each cut cleanly through, lying on a dusty wooden floor under a bed frame.
Two plain kitchen tumblers on a nightstand, each with a dried cloudy orange film in the bottom.
A hospital laboratory report form with a printed header and typed results, illegible, on a kitchen table.
A photocopy of a typed letter in capitals, illegible, with a faint ink stamp in the top corner that reads exactly "COPY", lying on a cream Formica kitchen table.
A police witness statement form, several typed pages stapled, with handwritten notes in the margins, illegible.
A page torn from a small pocket notebook, careful block capitals in pen, illegible, with a note clipped to it.
A typed letter in capitals and its plain white envelope with a postmark, illegible, under a glass paperweight.
A blank cassette tape in a clear plastic case beside a small portable cassette player and a folded typed transcript.
A carbon copy of a telephone company call record with columns of numbers, illegible, with a handwritten note clipped on.
A second typed letter in capitals with its envelope, illegible, on a newsroom desk.

A folded small-town broadsheet newspaper, slightly yellowed newsprint with a soft crease. Printed exactly as written, sharp and easy to read: the masthead in an old-fashioned blackletter typeface, "MARIPOSA BAY COURIER"; a small line under it, "THURSDAY, OCTOBER 13, 1988"; and the main headline in very large heavy black condensed capitals on two lines, "POLICE: KIDNAPPING CLAIM" on the first line and "APPEARS STAGED" on the second. The headline is circled by hand in red grease pencil. Below it, a black and white news photo of a small stucco house with a sedan out front and a smaller portrait photo of a woman in her late twenties with brown shoulder-length hair. The body columns are small and unreadable.
Several typed pages of a personal statement, signed at the bottom, illegible, on a dining table beside an electric typewriter.
A pair of cheap children's swim goggles with a blue rubber strap, both lenses covered in black electrical tape.

A cork board with two cards pinned side by side among other soft, unreadable notices. On the left, a hand-lettered white index card in neat block capitals that reads exactly "TV - RADIO - STEREO REPAIR / FAIR PRICES. HOUSE CALLS. / G. PELL, CABIN 14 / LEAVE WORD AT THE STORE", on four lines where the slashes are. On the right, a small printed card with a border of little pine trees that reads exactly "PINE RIDGE LUMBER CO. / THE MILL WHISTLE SOUNDS AT 12 NOON / MONDAY TO FRIDAY", on three lines where the slashes are.
An open green clothbound store ledger with handwritten entries and signatures, illegible.
A suburban police crime report form, typed, several pages, illegible, in a manila envelope.
A paging company subscriber record form, typed, illegible, beside a small black pocket pager.
A sheriff's search warrant inventory, several typed pages, illegible, in a sealed evidence envelope cut open.
A crime laboratory report with typewritten letters side by side under a magnifying loupe, illegible.
A small portable cassette recorder with an external speaker, a cassette beside it whose paper label is handwritten in pen and reads exactly "MSG", next to a typed sheriff's transcript, illegible.
A polygraph chart printout with wavering lines and a typed summary sheet, illegible.
A bank withdrawal slip half out of a white bank envelope, its printing illegible, with a small scrap of notepaper beside it covered in a few lines of hurried pen handwriting, illegible.
A county crime laboratory bench note, typed, illegible, clipped to a folder, with two glass tumblers in evidence bags.

Southern California in 1988. Along the left edge and the bottom, the Pacific coastline in pale blue: a small coastal town on the coast at the far left a third of the way down, and a harbor city on the bottom coast just right of center. A large city grid fills the center, slightly below the middle. To the right of the city, a broad valley of small towns. Across the top right corner, green pine-covered mountains with a small lake near the top right. Highways in ochre link the coast town, the city, the valley and the mountains.

A Benedictine abbey in a rain-dark Yorkshire dale at dusk, painted as a manuscript miniature: a squat bell tower against a gold-leaf sky, a cloister walk lit by one lamp, and in the foreground a small vaulted room whose oak door stands forced open, a single bronze candlestick missing from the ring of wax on the desk inside. Down the hillside a boy in a black novice's cloak wades a swollen beck toward a watermill. The left third of the image is quiet sky and moor.

images.subject: A Yorkshire dale in 1327. In the upper middle an abbey church with a bell tower; just below it a square cloister with buildings around it (chapter house and infirmary to the right of the cloister, the cellarer's range and a kitchen court to its left, an abbot's lodging below right); a guest-house and a gatehouse in the wall at lower left; a precinct wall around it all. A beck flows from the top right down the right side, with a small watermill on it at the right a little below the middle. A manor house with a hall on the moor in the upper right. Brown moorland, green fields, a road from the gate down the lower left.

A quiet street of brick row houses in a small western Pennsylvania steel town on a rainy autumn night in 2018. On the right, a large oak at the curb with a pale fresh gash in its bark at bumper height; at its foot, a small roadside memorial of glass candle jars glowing in the rain, a few wilted flowers and a child's stuffed rabbit. Across the street, one brick house with its porch light on and a woman in a cardigan standing alone on the top step, half in shadow, looking down the street. Far down the block, at the corner under a sodium-orange streetlight, the red taillights of a dark full-size SUV turning away, a tiny amber glow inside its dashboard. Wet asphalt reflecting the candles and the streetlight, steam rising from a storm drain, smokestacks of an old mill faint against the clouded sky. The left third of the image is quiet dark rain, brick and sky.
Tired, grieving but composed; a quiet, steady expression.

images.subject: Change ONLY the mouth: the lips are parted slightly, about the width of a pencil, as if in the middle of saying a soft "t", "d" or "n" sound. The tips of the upper teeth are just visible; the jaw drops only a little. The lips stay relaxed, not smiling.

Change ONLY the mouth and the chin just below it: the mouth is open in the middle of saying "ah", as in "father". The jaw drops naturally and the lips open about the width of two fingers in a relaxed oval, the upper teeth and the tip of the tongue just visible. Ordinary speech, not a shout or a smile.

Change ONLY the mouth: in the middle of saying "ee", as in "see". The lips are pulled slightly wider at the corners and only a little apart, showing both rows of teeth lightly together or nearly together. The jaw is almost closed. Not a smile: the corners do not turn up and the cheeks do not lift.

Change ONLY the mouth and the chin just below it: in the middle of saying "oh", as in "go". The lips are rounded into a soft, open oval, taller than it is wide, the inside of the mouth dark with only a hint of the upper teeth. The jaw drops a little. Ordinary speech, not surprise.

Change ONLY the mouth: in the middle of saying "oo", as in "who". The lips are pushed slightly forward and gathered into a small, round, puckered opening, smaller and tighter than "oh". No teeth showing. The jaw is nearly closed.

Change ONLY the eyes: both eyes are fully closed in a natural, relaxed blink, the upper lids all the way down and meeting the lower lids, the lashes resting along the lid line, the lids smooth and calm, not squeezed. The eyebrows stay relaxed and the mouth stays gently closed.

Bellwether, a small fictional steel town on a river in western Pennsylvania in 2018, and the edge of Pittsburgh. A broad pale blue river enters at the top right corner, where a dense city grid sits, and curves down the right side to the bottom right. Along its near bank in the lower right, an old industrial riverfront of rail lines and empty lots. The town's small downtown grid sits just above the center. Residential streets of small blocks spread across the left and center, with a cul-de-sac neighborhood a little below the center right. A highway in ochre runs from the lower left corner up toward the center. A road runs from the downtown to a county complex in the upper right. Green hillsides and parkland fill the gaps.
images.suffix: A hand-painted street map, seen flat from directly above and filling the whole image edge to edge like a sheet laid on a table: no table, no border, no frame. Muted map colors: cream paper, ochre streets, sage green parkland, pale blue water, faint fold creases. Absolutely no words, letters, numbers, street names or symbols anywhere on the map.

images.subject: A police crime scene photo board: three glossy color photographs pinned side by side, a silver Honda CR-V with its front end against an oak tree at night, airbags deployed and the driver's window shattered; a row of bullet holes in its driver's side door and pillar at window height; and a dent about 14 inches long with dark gray paint streaks on its left rear quarter panel at bumper height. Below them, a hand-drawn scene diagram with soft, unreadable notes.
A preliminary autopsy report on a county medical examiner's letterhead, two stapled pages on a steel desk, soft unreadable typed text, a paper clip and a pen.
A small thermal-paper gas station receipt lying on a counter, curling slightly, soft unreadable print, with handwriting in blue pen on the back showing through faintly.

A computer monitor in a dim back office showing a grainy color still from a gas station security camera at night: fuel pumps under a bright canopy with no car at them, and at the dark far edge of the lot a dark full-size SUV pulling out with its headlights on, a tiny amber light glowing on the left of its dashboard and two dim figures behind the windshield. A timestamp in the corner reading exactly: 09/14/2018 21:52:02.

A curved piece of black textured plastic vehicle wheel-arch trim about six inches long, with two broken mounting clips, flecks of dark gray paint along one edge and a smear of silver paint on the other, lying in an evidence bag on a lab table beside a ruler.

A police evidence tray holding spent brass cartridge cases in two separate groups, seven on the left and five on the right, each beside a small numbered yellow marker, with a typed report beside the tray in soft, unreadable text.

A photograph looking across a residential street from a brick house's front steps at eye level: an oak tree with candles at its foot under a streetlight in plain view, and to the right a tall privet hedge hiding the street beyond a bend.

A police property inventory form on a clipboard with soft, unreadable typed lines and a handwritten note at the bottom, beside two wallets, two phones, a set of keys and a carnival wristband in clear plastic evidence bags.
A small spiral pocket notepad with a company logo, lying open, its last pages covered in hurried ballpoint handwriting, soft and unreadable except for one underlined word reading exactly: ORANGE.
The first page of an environmental assessment report on consultant letterhead, with a red RECEIVED rubber stamp, soft unreadable typed text and a data table with one row circled in red ink.

An environmental assessment report page in a three-ring binder with a colored tab, soft unreadable typed text, the lower paragraphs in a very slightly different typeface and spacing from the rest of the page.

Pages from a surveyor's field book: columns of handwritten coordinates in soft, unreadable pencil and a pencil sketch of a rectangular building outline with five small circles marked around it and one small circle inside it, a north arrow and wavy lines for a river along the bottom.
A printed accounts payable ledger page on a desk, columns of soft unreadable payments, with a pencil question mark in the margin next to one line.
A single printed invoice on a security company's letterhead, mostly empty space, a single line item and a total in soft unreadable type, lying in a wire tray on top of other invoices.

A brown nine-by-twelve envelope, opened, with RACHEL handwritten on the front in marker; spilling out of it, photocopied report pages, a handwritten note on notepaper and a small black USB flash drive.
A computer printout of a document history log with soft unreadable rows, paper-clipped to a photocopy of a handwritten visitor sign-in book page and a small handwritten sticky note.
A paper wall calendar pinned to a refrigerator door, turned to October, with a photo of a high school marching band at the top and handwriting in a few of the date squares, soft and unreadable.

A black and white marbled composition notebook lying open on a kitchen table beside a mug, its page covered in neat handwriting, soft and unreadable, with a small sketch of a car's dashboard and a circled number 4.

A photograph of the front hall of a house at night taken from the threshold: the front door half open, a ceramic lamp on its side on the runner, reading glasses on a beaded chain on the floor, a dark smear on the door frame, a muddy boot print on the doormat.
A forensic laboratory report on a county letterhead beside a sealed swab tube and a DNA profile printout with colored peaks, soft unreadable text.

A photograph of a dark gray SUV on a gravel road beside a rusted rail spur, inside yellow police tape, its rear windows soot-blackened from a fire, a red gas can in the gravel. On the rear hatch, white lettering reading exactly, on two lines: BELL SECURITY / UNIT 4.

A laptop on a lab bench showing a digital street map with a route drawn in a red line between four pin markers, a table of times beside it in soft, unreadable text, a small black telematics box with wires beside the laptop.
A bank transaction record printout beside a white bank cash envelope in a clear evidence bag, soft unreadable print.
An open laptop on a dining table at night, its screen showing an email draft window with a few paragraphs of soft, unreadable text, the room around it dark.

A whiteboard on a garage wall with a handwritten fleet list in marker and a printed duty roster pinned beside it, one name on the roster crossed out and another written over it in thick black marker, soft and unreadable.

A body shop repair invoice on a clipboard, soft unreadable typed lines and a handwritten technician's note at the bottom, beside a new black plastic wheel-arch trim part still in its plastic wrapping.

A comparison microscope view split down the middle, showing two cross-sections of layered automotive paint, gray over primer, side by side and matching, with a printed lab report beside the microscope.
A laptop screen in a cramped trailer office showing a towing dispatch app: a list of calls on the left in soft unreadable text and a small map on the right with a GPS dot parked at one location.
Phone company call records, three printed pages fanned out on a police desk, soft unreadable rows of numbers with a few lines highlighted in yellow.
A bank wire transfer confirmation slip with a printed email paper-clipped behind it, in an open bank folder, soft unreadable text.

Three grainy printed security camera stills laid out side by side: a dark SUV turning onto a gravel road at night, a lone figure in dark clothing walking along a road, and a white pickup truck leaving a gate. Each has a small timestamp in the corner, soft and unreadable.
A pair of worn leather work gloves and a cracked smartphone in a blue case, each in a clear evidence bag with a red seal, beside a DNA profile printout on a lab bench.

The abandoned East Mill of a steel works on a river at dusk in the rain, a chain-link gate with police tape in the foreground, one brick maintenance building inside with a single work light glowing in a ground-floor window. A young woman's faded 1996 senior portrait is taped to the gate. The left third of the image is quiet gray sky and river mist.

Hollow Creek, a small fictional steel town on the Monongahela River in western Pennsylvania, in 2018. A broad brown river runs across the lower right; along its near bank the long rusted sheds of a closed steel works, its West End near the center bottom and its East Mill toward the right. The town's small downtown grid sits just left of center, with brick row-house streets around it and a hillside of houses above. A county highway in ochre runs from the upper left; a dirt road climbs into wooded ridges at the bottom left. Painted as a hand-drawn local map with no readable labels.
A direct, amused look, as in a 1995 senior portrait.
images.suffix: A painted head-and-shoulders portrait made for a talking portrait. The person faces the viewer directly, head straight and level, looking straight into the camera, mouth gently closed with the lips relaxed, not smiling. Head centered horizontally, face filling the upper middle of the frame, shoulders across the bottom. Nothing covers the mouth or eyes: no hands near the face, no hair across the lips. Even, soft lamplight from the front and slightly above, so both sides of the face are clearly lit. Plain, dark, muted painted backdrop, a little warmer behind the head. Natural, believable face; not a caricature.

Even, soft lamplight from the front and slightly above, so both sides of the face are clearly lit. Plain, dark, muted painted backdrop, a little warmer behind the head. images.subject: A yellowed 1996 police missing person form on a desk, typed in a typewriter font, a school photo of a young dark-haired woman clipped to the corner, under a desk lamp.

A 1996 drugstore color snapshot, slightly faded: a smiling young woman with dark hair in the driver's seat of a blue 1987 Chevrolet Cavalier, seat pulled close to the wheel, door open, summer evening.
A spiral notebook with a worn cardboard cover lying open on a bedspread, blue ballpoint handwriting, one page torn out at the binding.
A 1996 bank wall calendar turned to August, river photograph above the grid, handwriting in some squares, one square written in hard pressed ink.
A punched paper time card and a small spiral darkroom log on a darkroom counter under a red safelight, trays and a copy stand behind.
Two black and white 8x10 photographic prints of a typed office memo, with a handwritten note at the bottom, half out of an orange photo studio envelope.
Photocopied yellow legal pad pages of a detective's slanting handwritten notes, clipped together in a manila folder.
A 1996 police tow and inventory form with a parking ticket stapled behind it, on a clipboard, a blue compact car in a tow lot blurred in the background.
A typed 1996 witness statement form with a signature at the bottom, coffee ring on the corner.
A typed 1996 witness statement form with a handwritten note in the margin.
A typed 1996 witness statement form, a small hand-drawn sketch of a road and gate in the margin.
A modern printed police incident report on a desk beside a laptop, a photo of a rusted industrial building paper-clipped to it.
Police scene photographs and a measured sketch of a small caged tool room pinned to steel mesh, evidence markers, work-light glare.
A rusted steel door hasp with a broken short weld bead, a heavy chain through the handle held by an old brass padlock rusted shut, wooden pallets leaning nearby, police evidence tags.

A worn women's denim jacket laid on a steel exam table beside a gold high school class ring with a red stone, a brass key on a paper tag, folded newspaper clipping and a few dollar bills, evidence bags.
A forensic anthropology report on a clipboard beside a gloved hand and calipers, a lab light box glowing behind, no remains visible.
Two dental x-ray films side by side on a light box with a report form beneath.
A grease-stained 1996 taxi driver's daily trip sheet, handwritten rows of fares, in a cardboard archive box.
Two pages of handwritten lined paper on a kitchen table beside a mug of coffee, signed at the bottom.
A black 1990s pager rubber-banded to a 3x5 index card with neat handwriting, on top of a cardboard box of keepsakes.
A 1996 corporate incident report with a press release clipped to it, in a dusty records carton, abandoned office.
A 1996 union grievance form with handwritten complaint text and an initial stamp, in a green file folder on a union hall table.

A bound green ledger lying open to a page of neat handwritten dated entries, one entry in darker blue ink than the rest, and a white paper OSHA copy tab sticking out from the page edge with words that read exactly "OSHA 6/24/96"; all other writing soft and unreadable.
A carbon work order form with a priority crossed out and rewritten, a red tag stub stapled to it, in a three-ring binder.
A typed shift roster with a tool room sign-out sheet clipped behind it.
A manila envelope with three office papers sliding out: a photocopied memo with a handwritten note, a carbon copy memo, a carbon letter, a short handwritten note on the envelope.
A government inspection summary with a federal seal header on a gray archive table under fluorescent light.
Handwritten statements on union letterhead, a pencil and an old cassette recorder beside them.
A photographic contact sheet and enlargements of a dim industrial gas valve room: a large fan motor with a red danger tag wired to it, a wall monitor panel with a dark display.
A narrow underground valve gallery under a steel furnace, rusted valves in a row, three wall sensor heads, a seized fan with a scrap of red tag, a brass memorial plate on the rail, flashlight beam.
Typed 1996 meeting minutes on company letterhead, initialed at the bottom, lying in a plain manila folder; all text soft and unreadable.
A single folded ledger page with handwritten entries and a small handwritten slip clipped to it, lying in the hidden compartment of a green metal tackle box.
A banded stack of identical printed safety bulletins in an open steel desk drawer, a faded sticky note on top.
A confidential 1996 executive bonus schedule page in a Human Resources file folder, typed text soft and unreadable, with a red payroll rubber stamp across the bottom that reads exactly "PAID".
A thick recorded real estate agreement in a deed book binder, a clause flagged with a paper strip.

Two 1996 letters laid side by side in a borough file folder: a typed letter on union letterhead with a blue rubber stamp that reads exactly "RECEIVED APR 17 1996" and a penciled "LG" beside it, and a short typed borough reply; all other text soft and unreadable.
A typed question and answer interview summary in a government binder.
A short typed borough memorandum on letterhead, signed, in the same file folder.
A bound medical treatment logbook open to handwritten entries, an oxygen mask and an old stretcher in a dim first aid room.
A 1990s audio cassette in a clear case with a paper label handwritten in ink that reads exactly "E. HAYES, 3/98", and a portable cassette player beside it, on a newsroom desk piled with clippings.
A 2018 desk answering machine with a blinking message light on a cluttered office desk.

A hardware store wall calendar turned to October 2018 on the side of an almond-colored refrigerator, held by a magnet shaped like a bass fish, handwritten notes in several squares that are soft and unreadable, and printed at the top of the grid the words that read exactly "OCTOBER 2018".
A police photo board of a storage unit scene: shelving, dumped file boxes, an overturned green tackle box, evidence markers; no visible body.
An autopsy summary report on a clipboard on a steel counter, gloves and a pen.

A laser-printed gate keypad access report on plain white paper, rows of time-stamped entries in a table that are soft and unreadable, lying on a self storage office counter beside a 2016 computer keyboard.
A two-page security services contract with a signature, in an open filing cabinet drawer.
A stack of printed phone call detail records with a few lines highlighted in yellow.
A typed police witness statement with a signature, on a detective's desk.
A police property inventory form on a desk with two typed column headings that read exactly "MISSING" and "LEFT BEHIND", the lines below them soft and unreadable, a pen beside it.
A partial lug-soled boot print pressed into spilled motor oil on a concrete floor, a yellow evidence marker numbered 6 and a casting frame.
A handwritten letter on lined paper and a stamped, addressed, unsealed envelope on a wooden desk in a den.
A clipboard with a handwritten security patrol log sheet, hanging on a nail in a construction site trailer, a radio charger below.
A framed company vehicle and equipment roster beside a state security license certificate on a paneled office wall.
A typed police interview summary on a desk, a detective's notes in the margin.
A pink carbon garage work order slip clipped in a metal rack in an auto repair shop, its handwriting soft and unreadable, with a red rubber stamp across it that reads exactly "PAID CASH".
A green clothbound ledger lying open on an office desk, handwritten rows of invoices.
Printed mobile phone call records with three lines highlighted, a court order cover sheet.
A bank wire transfer confirmation printout with a bank logo header.
A modern police incident report on a desk under a lamp.
A state police lab report beside a plaster cast of a boot print and a black tactical boot in an evidence bag.
The same desk answering machine, message light blinking, a rainy window behind.
A modern missing person report with a driver's license photo of a gray-haired man in glasses.
A suburban front hall: eyeglasses on the floor with one lens out, a rumpled runner rug, a coat and cap on a rack; a cold untouched dinner plate visible in the kitchen beyond.

Two plastic weekly pill organizers side by side on a kitchen counter by a coffee maker, each with two rows labeled with printed words that read exactly "AM" and "PM": the first almost empty with only its last evening compartment still full of white tablets, the second freshly filled; three orange prescription bottles with white caps stand beside them.

Four black and white night-vision doorbell camera stills printed on paper: a full-size pickup truck with a roof light bar pulling into a driveway behind a parked sedan, a large dark figure at a front door, two figures crossing to the truck, and the truck backing out with its rear license plate blurred so that only the characters that read exactly "ZK" and "71" and "4" can be made out.
A law firm letter on heavy paper with a penciled note across the bottom, on a dining table, an empty coffee can on the shelf behind.
Printed home phone call records with a few lines highlighted.
A printout of license plate reader hits with small grainy camera images of a black pickup on a rural highway at night.
Printed state corporation records for an LLC on a courthouse counter, a stamp and a pen.
A county tax parcel record and a tax map with a dirt road highlighted, on a records counter.
A rusted pipe gate on a muddy forest road at night, an old chain with a bright new brass padlock, fresh tire tracks through puddles, flashlight beam.

A stone-walled cellar under a cabin with a dirt floor: a folding cot with a sleeping bag, cut black zip ties on the floor and one still looped through an eye bolt in the wall, a plastic bucket, water bottles, a dead battery lantern, a white handkerchief by the steps, and scratched into a wooden beam above the cot the letters and numbers that read exactly "LG 10/29".
An open coffee can on a shelf above a wood stove holding a black leather wallet, a steel wristwatch and a small brass key.
A court search warrant return form listing seized items in soft unreadable type, beside a gas station fuel receipt with soft unreadable print sealed in a clear evidence bag.
A typed police supplementary report on a desk, morning light.
A hospital physician's summary on letterhead on a clipboard at the foot of a hospital bed.
A multi-page signed police statement on a hospital tray table beside a water cup.
A photocopied union letter with a small handwritten borough routing slip stapled to it, on a bank safe deposit box tray.
A typed custodial interview summary with a rights waiver form beside it.
A cheap gray prepaid flip phone in an evidence bag on top of a printed call log report.
Printed scans of three handwritten letters signed W., under a printed email, on the field office desk.
A large bound purchase ledger open on a dusty weigh office counter in an abandoned rail building, a big platform scale behind.
A 1996 punched time card on top of a shoebox of old pay envelopes in a basement.
A garage invoice book open to a 1995 page with a snapshot pinned to it of a dark blue small pickup with a black ladder rack.
A thick 1996 telephone directory open to the business listings, a finger marking one line.
Two handwritten pages signed at the bottom, on a kitchen counter, a tissue box beside them.
A typed police interview summary with a detective's handwritten note at the bottom.
A bound security gate log open to a page of hourly handwritten entries with supervisor signatures, in a small concrete guardhouse.
A carbon expense report and a hotel folio photocopy with a handwritten note clipped on.
A framed state grant award letter on a reception wall beside an architect's rendering of riverfront apartments.
A detective's typed financial summary table with bank statements fanned beneath it.

A white envelope with handwriting on its front that reads exactly "For Blackwood. Friday.", tucked inside the front cover of an open black leather family Bible on a bedside table beside a brass reading lamp.
A recorded deed page in a large deed book, a one dollar consideration line flagged.
A small bank savings passbook open to a deposit line with a check stub stapled in.
A bound garage parts ledger open to a handwritten August 1996 page with a margin note, a coil of chain and an old portable welder in the dim loft behind.
A heavy steel workbench with an angle-iron front edge under harsh police work lights, a vise, copper strippings in the dust beneath, an evidence swab tag.
Bundles of stripped copper wire tied with wire and hung with paper parts tags, stacked behind plywood in a dusty industrial loft, rusted wire strippers beside them.
A small folded sheet of 1990s company letterhead with a short fountain pen note, on a bank box tray.
A questioned documents lab report beside handwriting samples under a magnifier.
A short typed expert opinion letter on medical examiner letterhead beside a plaster cast of a straight metal edge.

A private investigator's office at night, lit by one green-shaded desk lamp. In the middle-right of the frame stands a large cork board on a wheeled black metal frame with casters, covered in pinned documents, photographs, receipts and index cards, joined by red string into six separate clusters that all run toward one empty spot in the center of the board where a single pushpin holds nothing. On the desk in front of it, a small scattered pile of old tarnished silver coins catches the lamplight. Rain streaks a tall window behind, with the faint lights of a city. The left third of the image is quiet dark office wall and shadow. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A small-town Pennsylvania nonprofit's office on a rainy November night, seen through a second-floor window of an old brick building. Inside, one desk lamp is still on. The desk is in disarray: a drawer pulled out and forced, papers scattered on the floor, a filing cabinet hanging open, and a clean empty rectangle in the dust on the desk where a heavy ornament used to sit. On a bookshelf behind, one thick old accounting reference book sits slightly out of line with the others. Below the window, in the wet rear parking lot, a service door stands ajar and a plain white contractor's van idles with its lights off. The left third of the image is quiet dark brick and rain. No people. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

The sixth-floor corridor of an upscale Washington, D.C. hotel late at night, patterned carpet and brass wall sconces. In the middle-right, a guest room door stands open a few inches, warm light spilling out; through the gap you can see a suitcase still zipped on a luggage rack and a smartphone glowing face-up on a bedside table. The brass room number on the door reads exactly "614", printed exactly as written. At the far end of the corridor, a plain gray service door is propped open with a rubber wedge, a dim service elevator beyond. The left third of the image is quiet dark corridor wall and shadow. No people. The only readable text is "614". Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A Baltimore shipping container terminal at night in harbor fog. Towering gantry cranes fade into the mist above stacks of rust-red, blue and gray containers lit by sodium-orange floodlights. In the middle-right, in a narrow lane between two container stacks, a yellow hard hat lies upturned on the wet asphalt beside a tipped-over clipboard, and a heavy steel cargo bar leans against a container wall. One container door at the end of the lane stands slightly open, a sliver of light inside. The left third of the image is quiet fog, dark water and distant crane lights. No people. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A quiet cafe in Old Town Alexandria, Virginia, on a gray December morning. In the middle-right, a small window table set for two: one coffee cup half drunk, the other full and untouched, gone cold. Tucked under the sugar dispenser is a folded scrap of paper with one line handwritten in blue ink: "You're looking at the wrong people." printed exactly as written. Through the rain-streaked window, a cobbled brick street, and far down it a woman in a dark coat walks away carrying a small travel bag, too distant to make out. The left third of the image is quiet window, rain and brick. The only readable text is the handwritten note. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A private conference room off the ballroom of a grand Manhattan hotel during a charity gala in December. In the middle-right, a polished table with one chair knocked over, a glass of whiskey still standing, papers spilled across the carpet, and a bare spot on the table where a heavy marble desk piece used to sit. Through a half-open double door behind, the ballroom glows gold: crystal chandeliers, round tables in white linen, guests in evening dress as soft silhouettes, a distant podium. Snow falls past a tall window onto Manhattan lights. The left third of the image is quiet dark paneled wall. No identifiable faces. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

The inside of a corporate records archive the morning after a fire, late December. Long rows of metal shelving blackened by smoke, cardboard file boxes charred and collapsed, ash on the concrete floor, pale winter sunlight cutting through haze from a broken high window with snow on the sill. In the middle-right, one shelf stands untouched by the fire, and on it a single clean gap where one box was taken away before the flames, its dust outline still visible. The left third of the image is quiet smoke and shadow. No people. No readable text. Keep the main subject between the center and the right side of the frame so it still reads when cropped to a square.

A freestanding cork board on a wheeled frame, seen straight on: a brushed steel frame with bolted corners, two upright legs ending in black rubber casters, the cork a paler, cooler tan than an office wall board. A few pushpins and one short loop of red string on an otherwise bare surface, so whatever the player pins later reads clearly. No readable text.

images.subject: A police incident report on a clipboard: several typed pages, the top page headed in bold capitals that read exactly "CARROWAY POLICE DEPARTMENT" with the case number "18-1108-022" beneath it, the rest of the typed text soft and unreadable, and a short handwritten note in blue ink at the bottom of the last page, soft and unreadable.

Four glossy color crime scene photographs fanned out on a gray desk: a small office in disarray with a desk chair pushed back, a steel filing cabinet with two drawers open, a fan of black toner powder on carpet with a partial boot-sole print in it beside a photo scale, and a desk with a forced drawer. No body is visible in any photograph.

A medical examiner's typed summary on county letterhead, a single page with soft, unreadable text and a simple outline diagram of a head with a small triangular mark on its left side, on a steel table.

The corner of a wooden office desk in raking lamplight: a clean, dust-free rectangle about four by six inches in a fine film of dust where a heavy ornament stood, and above it on the wall a framed newspaper clipping of a smiling man in a tie holding a brass eagle on a walnut base.

An open drawer of a gray steel filing cabinet: green hanging files in a row with soft, unreadable tabs, and one empty hanging folder pushed apart from the others, its tab handwritten in neat square capitals that read exactly "FUND 2018, WORKING".

A printed building access control report on two sheets of plain white laser printer paper, columns of times and card numbers soft and unreadable except two lines highlighted in yellow marker, the highlighted text also soft and unreadable.
A county crime laboratory report beside a pair of well-worn tan leather work boots, one boot turned over to show a chevron lug sole with a worn outer heel edge, an evidence tag tied to its laces.
A typed police canvass statement form, a single page with a signature, soft unreadable text, a dog's leash lying across the corner of the page.

A paper desk-pad calendar whose header reads exactly "NOVEMBER 2018", the day squares covered in neat blue handwriting, soft and unreadable, one Friday square underlined twice, pens and a rubber stamp scattered across it.
A printed email on a desk, soft unreadable text, a few lines bracketed in pencil, beside a pair of reading glasses.

An old thick hardback book with a worn, faded green dust jacket lying open, the jacket slipped off to reveal a slim green clothbound columnar ledger hidden inside in place of the book's boards, its ruled pages filled with neat columns of handwritten figures in pencil and ink, soft and unreadable.

A brown accordion file with a handwritten label in black capitals that reads exactly "HOME COPIES", stuffed with photocopied payment vouchers each marked with a small red rubber stamp whose lettering is soft and unreadable, yellow sticky notes in neat handwriting stuck to several, soft and unreadable.

Four printed pages lying in the output tray of a small laser printer, the top page headed in bold capitals that read exactly "DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL", the rest soft and unreadable, a short handwritten note in pencil in the margin of the last page, soft and unreadable.
A sealed white envelope with a name handwritten on it in blue ink, soft and unreadable, lying in an open wooden desk drawer among sorted pencils and a box of staples.
A printed nonprofit grant register, long tables of soft, unreadable names and dollar amounts, three lines near the bottom circled in red pen.
A thick black ring binder lying open, a payment request form with a second invoice clipped behind it, soft and unreadable, a paper clip catching the light.
A printed state business filing certificate with an official seal, soft and unreadable typed fields, and a yellow sticky note in a neat old man's handwriting stuck to the corner.

A blue three-ring binder open to a stack of identical disbursement authorization forms, each with the same flowing signature at the bottom, two forms side by side with the same date, the text soft and unreadable.

A printed online banking payment confirmation on a leather desk tray, a coffee cup's ring stain on the page, the printed text soft and unreadable, and scrawled in black pen on the upper corner two words that read exactly "done. shred."
A bound contract with a cover page and a yellow plastic tab flag sticking out of one page, open to a dense page of numbered legal clauses, soft and unreadable.

A clipboard with a handwritten weekly job sheet in heavy block capitals, soft and unreadable, except that the end of the fourth line reads exactly "HOME", written in noticeably darker, heavier pen than the rest, a carpenter's pencil clipped beside it.
A white plastic building access card on a lanyard, a small printed credential record form beneath it with soft unreadable text and a handwritten note at the bottom.

Three grainy black-and-white security camera stills from above a bank drive-through lane at night: a white high-roof work van with a ladder rack in a small parking lot by two dumpsters, a lone figure carrying a bag toward a steel door, the van leaving. A vehicle registration printout beside them, soft and unreadable.
A small business bank statement on a cluttered steel desk, columns of small deposits soft and unreadable, one larger line highlighted, beside a coffee ring and a parts catalog.
A cell phone bill's call detail page, rows of times and phone numbers soft and unreadable, several rows highlighted in yellow, lying in a plastic mail tray.

Northern Virginia and Washington, D.C. from above. In the upper right, a broad pale blue river curves down from the top edge past a dense city grid with a circle of streets and a long green mall, and on its near bank a grid of high-rise blocks and suburban streets. Below them along the river's west bank, a compact old town of small blocks by the water, and further south a creek and an industrial park among woods. Highways in ochre run west from the city across the center: a big interstate out through suburbs and office parks to rolling farmland and wooded hills in the far left, where a small hamlet sits by a creek. A second road branches southwest to a new subdivision of curving cul-de-sacs. In the far upper left corner, a highway in ochre running off the edge of the sheet to the northwest, toward distant mountains.

The mid-Atlantic United States from western Pennsylvania to New York City, as a single illustrated travel map. On the far left, the city of Pittsburgh where three rivers meet. A turnpike in ochre runs east across wooded ridges and valleys; on a ridge in south central Pennsylvania, a small farm and a lane. Lower center, the Potomac River with Washington, D.C. on its north bank and the Virginia suburbs to the west and south, a small town of Frederick to the north, Silver Spring just above Washington, and Baltimore on the Chesapeake Bay to the northeast. Center right, Wilmington on the Delaware River. On the far right, the island of Manhattan and the edge of Queens across the East River. Pale blue water, soft green and tan land, fine roads, no readable text.

A grand Victorian Gothic stone estate on Halloween night seen from its open wrought-iron front gate, rain falling under a full moon through broken cloud. Steep gables, tall chimneys, ivy on the walls, every window glowing warm amber with candlelight. A wet curving drive reflects the light, low fog drifting across it, one dark late-model sedan parked near the front steps. Carved jack-o'-lanterns line the steps and sit by the gate pillar, a lit iron lantern on the pillar, red and orange autumn leaves overhead and on the ground. No people. No readable text.

images.subject: Change ONLY the mouth: the lips are parted slightly, about the width of a pencil, as if in the middle of saying a soft "t", "d" or "n" sound. The tips of the upper teeth are just visible; the jaw drops only a little. The lips stay relaxed, not smiling.

Change ONLY the mouth and the chin just below it: the mouth is open in the middle of saying "ah", as in "father". The jaw drops naturally and the lips open about the width of two fingers in a relaxed oval, the upper teeth and the tip of the tongue just visible. Ordinary speech, not a shout or a smile.

Change ONLY the mouth: in the middle of saying "ee", as in "see". The lips are pulled slightly wider at the corners and only a little apart, showing both rows of teeth lightly together or nearly together. The jaw is almost closed. Not a smile: the corners do not turn up and the cheeks do not lift.

Change ONLY the mouth and the chin just below it: in the middle of saying "oh", as in "go". The lips are rounded into a soft, open oval, taller than it is wide, the inside of the mouth dark with only a hint of the upper teeth. The jaw drops a little. Ordinary speech, not surprise.

Change ONLY the mouth: in the middle of saying "oo", as in "who". The lips are pushed slightly forward and gathered into a small, round, puckered opening, smaller and tighter than "oh". No teeth showing. The jaw is nearly closed.

Change ONLY the eyes: both eyes are fully closed in a natural, relaxed blink, the upper lids all the way down and meeting the lower lids, the lashes resting along the lid line, the lids smooth and calm, not squeezed. The eyebrows stay relaxed and the mouth stays gently closed.

The inside of an oak door: a heavy brass barrel bolt shot fully home, and on the carpet below it a brass keeper torn from the frame with a long splinter of oak still screwed to it.
A cast brass bookend shaped like a seated griffin lying on a dark carpet, a little blood caught in the angle of its square base, beside a yellow evidence marker.

A page torn from a small brown leather pocket notebook, lying beside the notebook, covered in hurried pencil notes in soft unreadable handwriting with a small pencil sketch of a head marking a spot above and behind the left ear, a short pencil lying across it.
The foot of tall dark oak bookshelves: a pale fresh curved scrape in varnished floorboards, and four empty screw holes with bright threads in the upright between two sections.
Narrow wooden stairs inside a wall, thick gray dust with a single clear line of a man's smooth-soled shoe prints going up and coming down, lit by a flashlight beam.

A new gray steel electrical disconnect box on an old cellar wall beside a slate fuse board, its big lever up, a printed label on the box reading exactly: MAIN HOUSE DISCONNECT. HOLLINS ELECTRIC 10/24/18. UP: ON. DOWN: OFF.
A small walnut-cased electric mantel clock with a plain dial, its plug cord trailing behind a vase.
A ruled index card on a green leather blotter, written in blue fountain pen in a small upright hand, soft unreadable text, beside a clean pale rectangle on the leather where a file used to lie.
A slate blue State Police laboratory folder, closed, a white label on the front reading exactly: LATENT PRINT REPORT, with a fingerprint card clipped to it.
A photocopied sheet of foundation letterhead with a handwritten numbered list of names in soft unreadable script, a lawyer's paperclip on the corner.

A single formal place setting at the foot of a candlelit table: silver, china, a half-finished soup plate pushed away, a water glass with a dark red lipstick mark, and a blank black-bordered place card.
Two pages of a yellow legal event pad in neat handwriting, soft unreadable text, signed at the bottom, a plain black ballpoint pen lying across them.

A cream seating chart card propped on a mahogany sideboard: a drawn long table with fourteen places, six down each side and one at each end, soft unreadable handwritten names in each, the place at the foot left blank with a short penciled note beside it in soft unreadable writing.
Three small glossy photo prints of a candlelit dinner table fanned out, in the first a woman in a black lace veil at the foot of the table.
A printout from a security system, a list of soft unreadable times beside small grainy camera thumbnails, one showing a veiled figure at a gate at night.

A woman's black lace evening glove, wrist length, lying on a patterned corridor runner, a tiny bead of dark red candle wax on one fingertip, the cuff turned back to show an old faded cloth name tag sewn inside with hand-inked capitals that read exactly "J. LISLE".
Three sheets of cream notepaper covered in handwriting in black ink, soft unreadable text, a wet ring from a water glass on one corner.
A red cloth-covered girl's diary from the 1990s lying open, round handwriting with little circles for dots, soft unreadable text.
A green clothbound foolscap ledger lying open, columns of figures in neat ink, with penciled notes in the margin, soft unreadable text.
Three slim brown buckram bound volumes of annual accounts stacked on a library table, one open, with an old archive request card sticking out of it.
A large photocopy of an old architectural floor plan drawing from 1903, fine ink lines of rooms and a narrow stair, soft unreadable lettering, held flat by two books.
A sheet of lined paper written slowly in big capital letters in ballpoint, soft unreadable text, signed at the bottom, a pair of reading glasses on it.
The back of a printed dinner menu card covered in careful handwriting, soft unreadable text, a small rosary lying across it.
A roll of architect's construction plans weighted open on a trestle with a tape measure and a brick, a section drawing of a pit and chamber, a yellow sticky note on it.
A small black leather shoulder bag from the 1990s and a tarnished silver bangle lying on a sheet of police evidence paper under a work light, beside a yellow evidence marker. Nothing graphic.
An old folded note on company letterhead in black ink, soft unreadable text, with a second handwritten sheet paper-clipped behind it, lying in the tray of a tin trunk among old letters.
A buff letter file stuffed with invoices, wedged in dust behind dusty bottles in a brick wine bin, the tab handwritten.
A sheet torn from a doctor's prescription pad, handwritten in black ink, soft unreadable text, two signatures at the bottom.
A ruled notebook hanging on a string beside a steel key cabinet, an open page of handwritten sign-out entries, soft unreadable text, one empty key hook above.
An electrician's carbon-copy work order form on a clipboard, with a printed header that reads exactly "HOLLINS ELECTRIC", soft unreadable handwritten entries below and two signatures at the bottom.
A handwritten letter on foundation letterhead in blue fountain pen, soft unreadable text, folded in thirds and opened out on a desk.
Three letters from a lender in window envelopes, one unfolded showing a bold red header and soft unreadable text, lying on an overnight bag.
Four letters in a woman's handwriting tucked into a medical journal on a night table, one unfolded, soft unreadable text.

A thick, much-handled brown accordion file with a neat typed label and below it the word "ANNABEL" written in a child's purple marker, papers and photocopies spilling from it, a handwritten card and a printed invitation card on top, an old typed police report beneath, all other text soft and unreadable.
An antique floor globe opened at the equator like a box, a heavy cream envelope lying inside it.
A small sheet of cream notepaper with a faint griffin watermark, unfolded, a few lines of block capitals in black ink, soft unreadable.
A State Police supplementary report on a clipboard, soft unreadable typed text, with a small evidence bag clipped to it holding a scrap of black satin ribbon with a silver edge.
The open door of a small iron stove, a grate full of black curled paper ash and one brown scorched corner of a printed invoice that did not burn.

A hand-drawn estate plan of a Victorian country house and its grounds, seen flat from above: in the middle, the outline of a large stone house with its rooms faintly marked; to the upper left, a carriage house; to the right, a greenhouse and a square yew hedge maze with a gate in the far boundary wall onto a lane; at the bottom left, a gatehouse at the end of a long curving drive; lawns, trees, a boundary wall all round. Cream paper, faded ink, a compass rose, a small title cartouche reading exactly: BLACKTHORN ESTATE.
images.suffix: A hand-painted estate plan seen flat from directly above and filling the whole image edge to edge like a sheet laid on a table: no table, no border, no frame. Muted colors: cream paper, faded sepia ink, soft greens for lawns and hedges.

Deep pine forest in the San Bernardino Mountains on a cool October afternoon in 1988, at standing eye level: tall ponderosa pine trunks with orange-brown bark, manzanita shrubs, fallen logs, and far back among the trees the dark roof of another small cabin. No people.

A mountain lake seen through tall pines on a cool October afternoon in 1988, at standing eye level: the trunks framing blue-gray water, and on the far shore a lumber mill with a tall brick smokestack and a small general store among the pines, a pale cool sky. No people.

A small isolated 1940s mountain cabin, 24 feet wide, 20 feet deep, 14 feet tall at the ridge, dark brown board-and-batten siding, a steep green asphalt-shingle roof with a stone chimney. Facing it: a plain wooden front door in the middle with one wide wooden porch step, a curtained window on each side of the door. On the left side wall, one window covered from the inside with a sheet of raw plywood. On the roof, an oversized television antenna on a 10-foot mast and a thin CB radio whip antenna, both held by guy wires, for a total height of 24 feet. The number "14" in small black metal numbers beside the door.
A neatly stacked woodpile of split pine logs, 8 feet long, 2 and 1/2 feet deep, 4 feet tall, a chopping block with an axe sunk in it at one end.

A late-1970s full-size cargo van with no side windows, completely covered by a brown canvas tarp pulled tight and weighted down with split firewood on the roof and along the sides, 17 and 1/2 feet long, 7 feet wide, 7 feet 9 inches tall. At one back corner the tarp has slipped up, showing dark blue paint and a blue California license plate with yellow characters that read exactly "2KXL418" with the word "CALIFORNIA" across its top.

A rectangle of yellow plastic barrier tape strung between four wooden stakes, 9 feet wide and 19 feet long, about 3 and 1/2 feet tall, enclosing flattened dirt with two tire ruts. The tape reads exactly "SHERIFF'S LINE DO NOT CROSS" repeated along its length in black letters.
A tall ponderosa pine, 70 feet tall, a straight trunk about 3 feet thick with orange-brown plated bark, bare for its lower half, a crown of long-needled dark green branches about 20 feet across.
A weathered wooden post 4 and 1/2 feet tall with a small board nailed across its top, hand-painted in white with a number that reads exactly "14".

A 1970s bedroom wallpaper: a small scattered pattern of tiny dusty rose and sage green flower sprigs on a cream ground, each sprig about an inch and a half across, spaced about 4 inches apart, slightly faded.
Low-pile wall-to-wall carpet from the 1970s in a soft sage green, a faint even texture, a little worn.
A round 1960s ceiling light about 14 inches across: a white glass bowl with a pattern of etched frosted flowers, held by a small brass finial in the center, switched off.
A 1960s six-panel interior door painted white, a brass knob on the right, in a plain white casing.
A 1960s solid flush wooden door to a garage, painted white, a brass knob and a brass thumb-turn deadbolt on the left, in a plain white casing.

A 1960s aluminum sliding bedroom window in a white painted casing, two panes side by side, both closed, pale green floral curtains pulled open to the sides. Every glass pane is completely transparent.
A framed botanical print of pressed wildflowers and grasses, 3 feet wide and 2 feet tall, in a thin pale oak frame with a cream mat.

The view from a bedroom window into the side yard of a suburban ranch house in the San Gabriel Valley on a gray, wet November morning in 1988 after rain: a narrow wet concrete path close below the window with a faint chalk circle about a foot across on it, nearly washed away, a strip of wet lawn, a hedge, and at the end of the path a wooden back gate in a 6-foot fence with its latch hanging loose, a dirt alley glimpsed beyond with tire tracks, sycamores and the gray San Gabriel Mountains in the distance under a low gray sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A 1970s queen bed with a white-painted wooden headboard, 5 feet 4 inches wide, 7 feet long, headboard 3 feet 10 inches tall, a quilted floral bedspread and blanket thrown back off the pillows as if someone got out in a hurry.
A 1970s white-painted wooden nightstand with one drawer and a small cabinet door below, 22 inches wide, 17 inches deep, 26 inches tall, a brass knob.

The base of a ceramic bedside lamp standing upright with no shade, glazed pale celadon green, 14 inches tall and 8 inches across, cracked clean through from top to bottom with one chip missing, a dark brownish smear on one edge, its brass harp bent.
A 1970s white-painted six-drawer dresser, 5 feet wide, 20 inches deep, 34 inches tall, brass bail pulls.
A tall stoneware vase, 14 inches tall, holding an arrangement of dried flowers: statice, eucalyptus and wheat stalks, about 20 inches tall in all.
An empty round dog bed in brown corduroy, 30 inches across, 8 inches tall, with a chewed rubber toy in it.
