Limewashed plaster over stone in a medieval English abbey guest-house, warm off-white with a faint cream tint, hand-trowelled and slightly uneven, a few hairline cracks and soft patches where newer limewash coats overlap; no pattern, the unevenness at a scale of about a foot.

Wide medieval oak floorboards, each board 10 to 14 inches wide and running the full height of the image, honey-brown to gray-brown oak worn smooth and paler along the middle, square wooden pegs instead of nails, narrow dark gaps between boards, a few knots and old scuffs.

A medieval timber ceiling seen from below: heavy square oak joists about 7 inches wide running in parallel every 2 feet, with plain gray-brown oak boards laid across them, the wood dark and aged, adze marks on the joists; no beams cross the other way.

A painted band at the foot of a limewashed wall, medieval English style: a flat band of red ochre limewash about 8 inches high with a thin darker red line along its top edge, the color slightly uneven and rubbed where feet and benches have scuffed it.

A medieval wall of coursed sandstone rubble, gray-buff and brown stones of mixed size, most 6 to 14 inches long, laid in rough level courses with wide joints of pale lime mortar; old, a little damp-stained at random, no plaster.

The underside of a plain medieval stone vault, seen straight up: rough limewashed rubble masonry, pale gray-white with the outlines of stones showing faintly through thin, flaking limewash, the stones about a foot across; no ribs, no fixtures.

Medieval sandstone flagstones looking straight down, rectangular slabs of varied size from about 18 by 24 inches to 30 by 36 inches laid in irregular courses, pale buff-gray stone worn smooth and slightly hollowed, thin dark joints, a few cracked corners.

A medieval wall of fine dressed ashlar, pale honey-gray sandstone blocks about 12 inches high and 18 to 30 inches long laid in level courses with very thin pale joints, faint diagonal tooling marks on each face, a few weathered and darker stones at random.

A medieval stone plinth course at the foot of an ashlar wall: one course of pale honey-gray sandstone about 12 inches high with a plain chamfered top edge sloping back, joints every 2 feet, the arris worn and slightly chipped.

A medieval English inlaid tile pavement looking straight down: square earthenware tiles about 5 inches across, red-brown with designs inlaid in pale yellow clay, alternating a fleur-de-lis and a four-petaled rosette within a circle, set square in rows with thin gray joints, the glaze worn through in places to bare red clay.

The underside of a medieval lean-to roof seen straight up: plain oak rafters about 5 inches wide set every 18 inches, running in parallel, with narrow gray-brown oak boards across their tops, the wood old and weathered gray, no cross beams.

A medieval hanging lamp seen from directly below, unlit: a round shallow bronze oil bowl about 10 inches across with a short spout, hung from three short iron chains that meet in a ring above it, the bronze dark and dull.

A medieval iron corona seen from directly below, unlit: a flat wrought-iron ring about 4 feet across with twelve small iron prickets around its rim, each holding a pale unlit beeswax candle, hung from four iron chains that meet at the center, the iron black and plain.

Wet medieval cobbles looking straight down: rounded gray and brown river stones about 4 to 6 inches across set tightly in packed earth, puddles of rainwater filling the low places, mud and a few wisps of straw in the joints.

A rough medieval undercroft floor looking straight down: uneven gray sandstone slabs of irregular shape, 12 to 24 inches across, set in packed earth, the joints wide and dark with grime, a few patches of old spilled lamp oil and scattered grains of salt and sawdust.

A medieval oak door seen straight on from inside the room, closed: a round-topped arched door of vertical oak planks, dark gray-brown, held by three long black iron strap hinges on the left side ending in curled tips, rows of square iron studs, a large black iron ring handle with a round backplate on the right side at waist height, set in a plain chamfered stone surround. No window.

A medieval floor candle stand, English, about 1320: a wrought-iron stand 4 feet 6 inches tall on three splayed feet spanning about 14 inches, a plain round shaft ending in an iron drip pan 5 inches across and a single pricket spike holding a tall unlit pale beeswax candle about 10 inches long. Black iron, plain and sturdy, in good condition.

A simple medieval wooden crucifix hanging on a wall: a plain oak cross about 2 feet tall and 15 inches wide, with a small carved and painted figure of Christ in a white loincloth, the cross's ends slightly flared, the paint softly worn.

A small medieval two-light window seen straight on: two narrow pointed lancet openings side by side under one stone arch in a plain chamfered stone frame, each light filled with small diamond-shaped quarries of thick glass held in a fine dark lead lattice, a plain oak shutter folded open against each side. Every pane of glass is completely transparent.

The view from an upper window of an abbey guest-house in Yorkshire on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327, looking across the outer court: wet cobbles and puddles, the stone gatehouse with its arch and slate roof on the left with an unlit iron lamp hanging by its arch, the square stone bell tower of the abbey church rising against a low gray sky on the right, and beyond the precinct wall the brown moor going up into cloud. Eye level about 14 feet above the court.

A wooden board hung on a wall, about 5 feet wide and 2 feet tall, of pale planed oak, with a long strip of cream parchment pinned along it by small iron nails. The strip is ruled with brown ink into seven equal spaces in a row, and small blank squares of parchment are pinned loosely along it. No writing.

A painted map of a Yorkshire dale on a stretched linen cloth hanging from a wooden rod by two cords, about 5 feet wide and 3 feet 6 inches tall, in a medieval manuscript manner: a little abbey church with a bell tower and a square cloister in the middle, a gatehouse and wall around it, a winding blue beck down the right side with a tiny watermill, a manor house on brown moorland at upper right, green fields, a road at lower left. No readable words.

A sturdy medieval English trestle table, about 1320: a thick plank top of pale oak 7 feet long, 3 feet 6 inches wide and 2 inches thick, set on two heavy oak trestles joined by a stretcher, total height 2 feet 6 inches. Plain, scrubbed and well used, a few knife marks and ink stains on the top, nothing on it.
A plain medieval oak bench, about 1320: a single thick plank seat 6 feet long and 14 inches wide on two slab legs with a cut-out arch at the foot, 18 inches high, gray-brown oak, worn smooth.

A tall medieval wooden reading lectern, English, about 1320: a sloped oak reading desk about 2 feet wide and 20 inches deep with a narrow ledge along its lower edge, on a turned central post with a cross-shaped foot, 4 feet 6 inches tall at the top edge of the slope. Dark oak, plain chamfered edges, nothing on it.

A narrow medieval guest bed, about 1320: a low oak bed frame 3 feet wide and 6 feet 6 inches long, 2 feet high, with a straw-filled mattress covered in coarse undyed linen, a gray-brown wool blanket folded at the foot and a plain linen bolster, neatly made.

A medieval English oak chest, about 1320: a plain plank chest 3 feet 6 inches long, 1 foot 9 inches deep and 2 feet high, dark brown oak bound with three black iron straps, a hasp and a small iron lock plate on the front, lid closed.

A small medieval wall fireplace, about 1320, unlit: a plain sandstone fireplace 5 feet wide, 2 feet deep and 7 feet tall with a sloping stone hood above a shallow hearth, a pair of iron fire dogs and a few split logs laid ready, no flames, the hood pale buff stone a little smoke-darkened at its mouth.

A medieval letter of commission, 1327: a sheet of cream parchment about 11 by 8 inches folded once and lying flat, with a round red wax seal about 2 inches across hanging from it on a narrow parchment tag. The writing is soft, unreadable brown Latin script.

A small medieval journal, about 1327: a book of parchment leaves about 7 by 9 inches and 1 inch thick, bound in plain brown limp leather with a flap and a leather thong wound around it, a white goose quill laid across the cover. Closed, lying flat.
A small folded medieval letter, 1327: a piece of cream parchment folded into a flat packet about 4 by 3 inches, sealed on the front with a blob of plain red wax with no device, lying flat.

A medieval written finding, 1327: a single sheet of cream parchment about 10 by 13 inches lying flat, covered in neat soft unreadable brown script, with a round red wax seal hanging from its foot on a short ribbon of red silk.

A medieval stone doorway seen straight on: a pointed arch in pale honey-gray sandstone with plain chamfered jambs and a hood molding over the arch, the door itself not shown. The whole doorway opening is completely transparent.

A small black iron hook bracket for a door bar, about 6 inches wide and 10 inches tall, hanging crooked from a stone wall by a single nail at its top, two empty nail holes below it with the lime plaster around them broken out, a few crumbs of plaster clinging to the stone.

A sheet of scrap parchment about 11 by 14 inches pinned at its top corners by two iron nails, upright, with a brown ink drawing of a small room seen from above: a desk under a window, a chest against the right-hand wall, a stool on its side between them and a figure lying on the floor between desk and chest, small notes around it in soft unreadable script.

A small medieval wall cupboard door set into a stone wall: a square door of oak boards about 17 by 19 inches in a plain wooden frame, with two small black iron butterfly hinges on the left and a little iron turn-button catch on the right, closed, the wood dark and smoothed by handling.

A medieval wall book press: a heavy oak shelf unit about 6 feet wide and 3 feet 6 inches tall fixed to a wall, two shelves holding large books bound in brown and red leather over boards with brass corner pieces, each book chained to an iron rod along the shelf front by a short iron chain, the books lying flat or leaning, no readable titles.

A narrow medieval lancet window in a thick stone wall, seen straight on: a single pointed opening about 2 feet 6 inches wide and 5 feet tall in a chamfered sandstone frame, glazed with small clear diamond quarries in a fine dark lead lattice, two iron bars across it. Every pane of glass is completely transparent.

The view from a small ground-floor window in the west range of a Benedictine abbey in Yorkshire on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: the wet slate roofs and stone chimney of the cellarer's range close by, a strip of muddy kitchen court below with a stack of firewood, and above the roofs the brown moor rising into low gray cloud. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A medieval English writing desk, about 1320: a heavy oak desk 5 feet wide, 2 feet 6 inches deep and 2 feet 7 inches tall, with a flat top whose back half rises in a gentle slope, a narrow pen ledge, and plank ends joined by a low stretcher. Dark oak, worn, with old ink stains; a small fresh dent near the left corner of the front edge. Nothing on it.

A great medieval cartulary register, about 1320: a large book about 18 by 13 inches and 4 inches thick, lying open, bound in brown leather over oak boards with brass corners and clasps, its parchment pages written in soft unreadable brown script with red initials, a wide stain of spilled black ink dried across the right-hand page.

A medieval iron-bound charter chest, about 1300: an oak chest 4 feet long, 2 feet deep and 2 feet 3 inches tall, its dark wood banded all over with black iron straps and studs, two iron carrying handles, with its lid standing open upright showing rolled and folded parchments inside, each with a small parchment tag, and a narrow leather-bound book lying on top of them.
A plain medieval three-legged stool, about 1320: a round oak seat 14 inches across on three splayed peg legs, 19 inches high, gray-brown oak, worn smooth.

A medieval oak door leaf on its own, about 1320, standing upright: vertical oak planks with a pointed-arch top, 3 feet 6 inches wide, 7 feet 6 inches tall and 3 inches thick, dark gray-brown, three black iron strap hinges along one edge, an iron ring handle and a simple iron latch on the other edge, the plank face around the latch bruised and splintered where it was forced.

A medieval swing bar for a door: a squared oak beam 4 feet 6 inches long and 4 inches square, gray-brown and smooth, with a black iron pivot eye through one end, and two small fresh pale scores across the grain on the top face of the free end.

A medieval cloister arcade seen straight on, about 15 feet wide and 9 feet tall: three pointed arches of pale honey-gray sandstone carried on slender paired round columns with simple molded capitals, standing on a low solid stone wall about 2 feet high. The openings of the arches above the low wall are completely transparent.

A wide open medieval archway seen straight on, about 10 feet wide and 9 feet tall: a broad pointed arch of pale honey-gray sandstone with plain chamfered edges, spanning between the walls of a cloister walk. The whole opening under the arch is completely transparent.

A low, narrow medieval door seen straight on, closed: oak planks with a slightly pointed top, 3 feet 6 inches wide and 6 feet 6 inches tall, banded across with four flat black iron straps, a black iron keyhole plate and a small ring handle on the right side, set in a plain chamfered sandstone surround. No window.

The view across the garth of a Benedictine abbey cloister in Yorkshire on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327, from the west walk looking east: a square of wet green grass with a round stone well with a wooden windlass in the middle, and across it the east walk's arcade of pointed arches under a slate lean-to roof, with the wide round-headed doorway of the chapter house in the middle of that walk, and the chapter house's stone gable and roofs rising behind under a low gray sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

The view along the south walk of a Benedictine abbey cloister on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a flagstone walk under a timber lean-to roof stretching away, a plain ashlar wall on one side with a large oak door to the refectory, and on the other side an arcade of pointed arches opening onto a wet green garth. Empty of people. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A long medieval stone bench, about 1300: a slab of pale honey-gray sandstone 8 feet long, 18 inches deep and 3 inches thick on three squared stone supports, 18 inches high, worn smooth on top.

A black wool novice's cloak of about 1327 folded into a neat square about 18 by 14 inches and 4 inches thick, with a small psalter bound in plain brown leather lying on top of it and a plain wooden spoon beside the psalter.

A medieval cloister window bay seen straight on, about 5 feet wide and 6 feet tall: an unglazed opening of two pointed lights divided by a slender sandstone column under one arch, in pale honey-gray chamfered stone. The openings are completely transparent.

The view from the north walk of a Benedictine abbey cloister in Yorkshire on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327, looking south across the garth: a square of wet green grass with a round stone well with a wooden windlass in the middle, and across it the south walk's arcade under a slate lean-to roof and the long stone refectory with tall windows rising behind it under a low gray sky. Eye level about 4 feet, as seen from a seat.

A medieval book cupboard set into a stone wall, seen straight on: a recess about 4 feet wide and 5 feet tall closed by two oak doors with black iron strap hinges and a small iron lock plate where they meet, the oak dark and plain.

A medieval monastic writing carrel, English, about 1320: a small open-fronted wooden booth of oak boards 5 feet wide, 3 feet deep and 5 feet 6 inches tall, with high side panels, a sloping writing desk built across it at 2 feet 8 inches, a fixed plank seat with a thin worn red wool cushion, a pot of goose quills and a horn inkwell set in the desk.

A small stack of medieval parchment sheets about 9 by 12 inches, written in a careful soft unreadable brown hand with small brown crosses in the margins, held down by a smooth round gray stone weight about 3 inches across.

A medieval reading stand with a book, about 1320: a sloped oak reading desk on a single turned post with a cross-shaped foot, 4 feet 2 inches tall and 22 inches wide, holding a thick book bound in brown leather lying open at two pages of large letters in soft unreadable script, a red thread lying across the pages as a marker.

A long medieval novices' desk, about 1320: a plain oak desk 8 feet long, 2 feet 6 inches deep and 2 feet 7 inches tall with a slightly sloped top, a fixed plank bench along one side, and on the desk several small hinged wooden wax tablets, a few practice sheets of scrap parchment and two bone styluses.

A tall medieval stained glass window of about 1300 seen straight on: three pointed lancets grouped under one arch in pale honey-gray stone tracery, about 10 feet wide and 16 feet tall, filled with silvery gray-green grisaille glass painted with fine leaf patterns, with a small round colored medallion in each lancet showing a saint in ruby red, blue and yellow glass. The glass is solid painted glass, not transparent.

A tall narrow medieval lancet window seen straight on, about 4 feet wide and 12 feet tall, in a chamfered honey-gray sandstone frame, filled with silvery gray-green grisaille glass painted with a fine pattern of trailing leaves and a narrow colored border of red and blue. The glass is solid painted glass, not transparent.

A medieval stone choir screen seen straight on from the choir side, about 20 feet wide and 14 feet tall: a solid wall of pale honey-gray ashlar with a row of blind pointed arcading carved across its upper half and a single central doorway with a pointed arch about 4 feet 6 inches wide and 8 feet tall. The doorway opening is completely transparent.

The view through a doorway in a choir screen into the nave of a Romanesque and early Gothic abbey church in 1327: a long stone nave with round piers and pointed arches, pale honey-gray stone, a tiled floor, and at the far end a great west door under a tall window of gray grisaille glass. Empty of people. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A medieval painted panel of the Virgin and Child, English, about 1300, hung on a wall: a gabled oak panel about 4 feet wide and 6 feet tall painted in tempera, the Virgin seated, crowned, in a blue mantle over a red gown, the Child on her knee, against a burnished gold ground in a red-painted frame.

A medieval sacristy door seen straight on, closed: a round-headed door of vertical oak planks, 3 feet 6 inches wide and 7 feet tall, dark brown, with two long black iron strap hinges with curled ends on the left, a black iron lock plate and ring handle on the right, set in a plain chamfered stone surround. No window.

A medieval inventory board hanging on a wall: a planed oak board about 20 inches wide and 30 inches tall, covered with a sheet of parchment written in columns of soft unreadable brown script, and below it a long narrow strip of parchment pinned on with small iron nails, with a few short lines of soft unreadable writing.

A medieval processional door between a church and its cloister, seen straight on, closed: a pointed-arch door of heavy oak planks 4 feet 6 inches wide and 8 feet tall, dark brown, covered with scrolling black iron hinge work across its face, a large ring handle on the right, set in a deep molded sandstone arch.

A medieval high altar, English, about 1300: a solid block of pale honey-gray sandstone 8 feet long, 3 feet 6 inches deep and 3 feet 4 inches tall with a thick projecting stone top slab, covered with a white linen cloth and a front frontal of deep red silk with a gold embroidered border, a plain gilt cross standing in the middle of the top and two tall unlit candles in silver-gilt candlesticks.

A run of medieval oak choir stalls, English, about 1300: five joined seats in a row, 12 feet long, 3 feet 6 inches deep and 5 feet tall, with tall carved armrests between seats, a high paneled back topped by a plain molded rail, and a continuous sloping book desk on a low paneled front. Dark oak, worn smooth.
A small medieval choir stall lamp, about 1320: a little bronze oil lamp with a round bowl 4 inches across on a short bronze stem and round foot, 9 inches tall, unlit, dark and dull with age.
A small wreath of fresh rosemary sprigs about 10 inches across, gray-green, loosely bound with a white linen thread, lying flat.

A small medieval side altar, English, about 1300: a stone block 6 feet long, 3 feet deep and 3 feet 4 inches tall, covered with a white linen cloth and a blue frontal with a border of small gold stars, a plain stone step at its foot.

A matched pair of medieval bronze pricket candlesticks of about 1300 standing side by side, each 1 foot 6 inches tall with a round domed foot about 6 inches across engraved around its edge with the letters "AVE MARIA", a knopped stem, a drip pan and an iron pricket spike. The left one holds a tall pale beeswax altar candle; the right one holds a short, thick, burnt-down candle. The right one's foot is dented on one side.

A medieval English painted plaster wall of about 1320: smooth warm off-white limewash painted with thin double lines of red ochre in a false-ashlar pattern, each painted block about 2 feet wide and 1 foot high in staggered courses, a small red five-petaled rosette in the center of each block, the paint softly faded.

A painted frieze band at the top of a medieval plaster wall, about 10 inches high: a running scroll of green vine stems and leaves with small red berries on a pale ochre ground, edged above and below with a thin red line, the paint slightly faded and worn.

A medieval two-light window seen straight on: two pointed lights side by side under a stone arch with a small quatrefoil opening above them, in a chamfered sandstone frame, glazed with small clear diamond quarries in a dark lead lattice, oak shutters folded open at each side, a plain stone window seat ledge below. Every pane of glass and the quatrefoil are completely transparent.

The view from an upper window of an abbot's lodging in a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: below, a walled orchard of bare, wet apple trees and a long fishpond, the slate roofs of the infirmary to one side, and beyond the precinct wall green fields running down to a swollen beck and brown moorland under low gray cloud. Eye level about 14 feet above the ground.

A fine medieval wall fireplace, English, about 1320, unlit: a pale sandstone fireplace 7 feet wide, 2 feet 6 inches deep and 9 feet 6 inches tall, with a tall projecting conical hood rising from a molded mantel shelf at 5 feet, carved corbels at each side, a pair of iron fire dogs and split logs laid ready on the hearth, no flames.

A small medieval carved wooden statue of a saint, English, about 1300: Saint Aldwyn seated on a bench, a book open on his knee and one hand raised, 16 inches tall, painted in faded red and blue with a gilt edge to his robe, a black Benedictine habit under the robe, on a small square base.

A good medieval oak table, English, about 1320: a thick oak top 6 feet long and 3 feet wide on two carved trestle ends with a pegged stretcher, 2 feet 7 inches tall, polished dark brown, covered half its length with a green wool cloth. Nothing else on it.

A medieval parchment account roll of 1327 lying half unwound: a long strip of cream parchment about 12 inches wide, rolled at one end, the open part about 2 feet long covered in columns of soft unreadable brown script with a small note squeezed into the margin, held flat by a small round pewter inkpot.

A medieval abbot's chair, English, about 1300: a carved oak box chair 2 feet 4 inches wide, 2 feet 2 inches deep and 4 feet 6 inches tall, with solid paneled sides, a high back carved with a pointed arch, and a flat red wool cushion on the seat. Dark oak.
A small medieval side table, English, about 1320: an oak table 3 feet long, 2 feet deep and 2 feet 7 inches tall on four plain square legs joined by low stretchers, dark oak, nothing on it.
A small pile of three folded medieval letters of 1327, each a parchment packet about 5 by 3 inches with a hanging wax seal: one green, one red and one brown. No readable writing.

A low, narrow medieval door seen straight on from inside a stone passage, closed: the plain back face of a door of vertical oak planks with a slightly pointed top, 3 feet 6 inches wide and 6 feet 6 inches tall, crossed by three horizontal oak ledges, a black iron latch bar and a small ring on the left, the wood dark and rough, set in a plain stone opening. No window.

The back of a small wall cupboard seen from a passage: a small square door of rough oak boards about 17 by 19 inches, unpainted and unfinished, with two small black iron hinges on the right and a wooden turn-button on the left, closed, a few fresh drips of pale tallow on the stone sill below it.

A rough, unfinished square timber frame set in a stone wall, about 2 feet wide and 2 feet 2 inches tall, roughly adzed pale oak with broken mortar at its edges where the opening was cut through, and one iron nail head standing proud of the left upright with a tiny tuft of black wool caught on it. The square opening inside the frame is completely transparent.

A medieval iron cellar hook hanging on a wooden peg driven into a stone wall: a straight black iron rod about 2 feet 6 inches long with a ring at the top and a curved hook at the bottom, the point of the hook rubbed bright, a tiny splinter of pale oak caught in the crook.

A medieval storage rack, English, about 1320: a rough oak shelf rack 5 feet long, 1 foot 7 inches deep and 5 feet 6 inches tall with three plank shelves, holding bundles of pale tallow candles tied with string, rolls of cream parchment tied with cord, and a few clay jars. Plain, sturdy, dusty.

A medieval oak cask of lamp oil, about 1320, standing upright: 2 feet across and 2 feet 7 inches tall, of dark oak staves bound with four split-willow hoops, a wooden bung in the top, the staves oil-stained near the bottom.

A medieval wooden crate of wine for the Mass, about 1320: a plain oak crate 2 feet 2 inches long, 1 foot 7 inches wide and 1 foot 5 inches tall, open at the top, holding six dark green glass flasks bound in straw, their necks stoppered with wax.

A wide medieval undercroft doorway seen straight on: a broad pointed arch of rough sandstone about 5 feet wide and 8 feet tall with plain chamfered jambs worn by carts, the oak door leaves not shown. The whole opening is completely transparent.

The view out of a cellar doorway into the kitchen court of a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a small cobbled court shining with puddles, on the far side the stone guest-house kitchen with a plank door and a shuttered window and a smoking chimney, a stack of firewood against a wall, and in the left corner a low iron-banded oak door in the end wall of the cloister range. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A black wool Benedictine habit of about 1327 hanging by its hood from a single wooden peg in a stone wall, the full-length habit about 4 feet 6 inches long falling straight, its right sleeve showing a small three-cornered tear neatly mended with new gray thread.

A medieval key board on a wall: a plank of oak about 2 feet wide and 18 inches tall with two rows of wooden pegs, a dozen large black iron keys of different sizes hanging from them, and a bundle of notched hazel tally sticks hung on a cord at one end.

A medieval timber partition, English, about 1320: a freestanding wall of vertical oak planks 10 feet long, 5 inches thick and 8 feet tall set in a heavy oak sill and head beam, with a plain plank door 3 feet wide near one end standing open, black iron strap hinges. Rough gray-brown oak.

A medieval cellarer's checker desk, English, about 1320: a plain oak desk 4 feet wide, 2 feet 2 inches deep and 2 feet 7 inches tall with a flat top and a small shelf beneath, scattered notched hazel tally sticks on its top, dark oak, ink-stained.
A medieval cellarer's day book of 1327: a narrow book about 8 by 12 inches bound in limp tan leather, lying open at a page of small neat columns of soft unreadable brown script and sums.

A small medieval wooden box of tally sticks, about 1320: a plain open-topped oak box 11 inches long, 7 inches wide and 6 inches tall, full of pale notched hazel tally sticks, each about 8 inches long.
A medieval merchant's balance, about 1320: a bronze beam balance 1 foot 6 inches tall on a wooden base 14 inches long, two shallow round bronze pans hanging on fine chains, the beam level.

A great medieval salt bin, English, about 1320: a heavy oak box 5 feet long, 2 feet 9 inches deep and 3 feet tall on short legs, of thick boards bound at the corners with iron, with a plain hinged wooden lid closed. Dark oak, the edges bleached and crusted white with salt.
A medieval cask of salt fish, about 1320, standing upright: an oak cask 2 feet across and 3 feet tall bound with willow hoops, the head closed, a white crust of salt along the staves.

A large medieval ale cask on its cradle, about 1320: an oak cask 4 feet long and 2 feet 6 inches across lying on its side on a low oak cradle, bound with willow hoops, a wooden tap in its head, dark oak with a damp stain below the tap. Total height 2 feet 10 inches.

One side of a small cobbled kitchen court in a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: the long two-story stone guest-house kitchen range with a slate roof and a tall stone chimney smoking, its ground-floor wall a plain stretch of rough sandstone rubble with no doors or windows in the middle part, wet and streaked with rain, under a low gray sky. Seen straight on at eye level, about 5 and a half feet.

One side of a small cobbled kitchen court in a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: the cellarer's range, a long low stone building with a steep slate roof and small shuttered upper windows, its ground-floor wall a plain stretch of rough sandstone rubble with no doors in the middle part, a gutter dripping, under a low gray sky. Seen straight on at eye level, about 5 and a half feet.

One side of a small cobbled kitchen court in a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: the plain west end wall of the cloister range in coursed sandstone rubble, its lower part a plain stretch of wall with no doors, above it a slate roof and beyond it the top of the square bell tower of the abbey church against a low gray sky. Seen straight on at eye level, about 5 and a half feet.

One side of a small cobbled kitchen court in a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a low rubble wall about 7 feet high with an open round-headed archway through to the wider outer court, through which the wet cobbles of the outer court and the stone gatehouse can be seen, and above the wall the brown moor rising into low gray cloud. Seen straight on at eye level, about 5 and a half feet.

A medieval kitchen door seen straight on from outside, closed: a plain door of vertical oak planks 3 feet 6 inches wide and 7 feet tall with a square top, weathered gray, two black iron strap hinges on the left, a wooden latch with a leather pull string on the right, a worn stone step at its foot, set in a rough stone opening. No window.

A small medieval kitchen window seen straight on from outside: a square unglazed opening about 3 feet 6 inches wide and 3 feet tall in a rough sandstone frame, a single oak shutter hinged at the top and propped half open on a stick, the inside behind it plain dark plastered wall.

A medieval court lamp on a wall, unlit: a black wrought-iron bracket projecting from the wall with a small iron and horn lantern hanging from its end, the lantern about 10 inches tall with a conical top and a ring, panes of thin pale horn.
A medieval rain butt, about 1320: a large oak tub 2 feet 2 inches across and 3 feet tall bound with willow hoops, standing upright, full of rainwater, a wooden dipper hanging on its rim.
A medieval stack of split firewood: logs of oak and ash about 2 feet long stacked neatly between two upright stakes, 6 feet long, 2 feet deep and 3 feet 6 inches tall, the bark gray and wet.

A medieval two-wheeled handcart, about 1320: an oak plank bed 3 feet wide and 4 feet long with low sides, two long handles extending 2 feet in front, two spoked wooden wheels 2 feet 6 inches across, standing level on a prop, empty, weathered gray. Overall 3 feet wide, 6 feet long and 3 feet tall.

A great medieval abbey gate seen straight on from inside, closed: two tall oak gate leaves under a pointed stone arch about 12 feet wide and 13 feet tall, made of heavy vertical planks crossed by horizontal ledges and studded with square iron nails, a small wicket door about 2 feet 6 inches wide and 5 feet tall set in the right leaf with its own ring handle, a heavy oak drawbar resting across both leaves in iron brackets.

A medieval gatehouse inner archway seen straight on: a wide pointed arch of pale honey-gray ashlar about 12 feet wide and 13 feet tall with a plain chamfered edge, no gate in it. The whole opening is completely transparent.

The view through an abbey gatehouse arch into the outer court of a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: wet cobbles and puddles, the two-story stone guest-house on the left, the long cellarer's range ahead, the great church with its square bell tower rising behind under a low gray sky. Empty of people. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A small medieval porter's lodge door seen straight on, closed: plain vertical oak planks 3 feet wide and 6 feet 6 inches tall with a square top, gray-brown, two iron strap hinges on the left and a wooden latch with a ring on the right, set in a chamfered stone surround. No window.

A small medieval porter's window seen straight on: a square opening about 3 feet across in a chamfered sandstone frame, closed by a single plain oak shutter with iron hinges at the top, and a broad stone sill below it.

A gatekeeper's roll hung on a wall: a narrow oak board about 18 inches wide and 3 feet 6 inches tall with a long strip of cream parchment pinned down its length, a line of heavy, careful soft unreadable brown writing for each comer, the lower end of the strip curling, a goose quill tucked behind a cord at the top.
A plain medieval porter's bench, about 1320: a thick oak plank bench 6 feet long, 16 inches deep and 18 inches high on two slab ends, weathered gray-brown.

The inside wall of a small medieval watermill: rough sandstone rubble thinly limewashed off-white, the stones showing through, irregular stones 6 to 14 inches across, dusted pale with old flour and streaked with damp; no pattern.
The beaten-earth floor of a medieval watermill looking straight down: hard-packed brown earth, smooth and uneven, dusted pale with spilled flour, a few scattered grains of wheat and wisps of straw.

A rough medieval mill ceiling seen from below: rough-hewn oak joists every 2 feet running in parallel with wide gray oak boards over them, the wood dusted white with flour, cobwebs in the corners of the joists.

A medieval mill doorway seen straight on: a square-headed opening about 4 feet wide and 7 feet tall with a heavy oak lintel and rough stone jambs, its plank door not shown. The whole opening is completely transparent.

The view out of a mill door at Hollin Bridge in a Yorkshire dale on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a muddy yard with a few sacks under a lean-to, a small stone bridge over a swollen brown beck, wet alder trees with yellowing leaves along the bank, a track leading up toward the distant abbey bell tower under low gray cloud. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A medieval mill wall opening seen straight on from inside: a square unglazed opening about 6 feet wide and 5 feet tall in a rough stone wall with a heavy oak lintel and sill, a plank shutter swung open to the left side. The opening is completely transparent.

The view through a mill wall opening at a medieval watermill wheel on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: close outside, a big undershot wooden waterwheel about 12 feet across with broad wooden paddles, wet and dark, turning in a swollen, fast, brown beck, foam on the water, alder trees on the far bank. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A small medieval mill window seen straight on: a square opening about 2 feet 6 inches across in a rough stone wall, closed by a plain gray oak shutter with two iron hinges, a flour-dusted stone sill.

A medieval water-driven millstone set, English, about 1320: a pair of gray gritstone millstones about 4 feet across enclosed in a round wooden tun casing 2 feet tall, with a square wooden hopper on a wooden frame above, a wooden spout at the side, and a short oak platform around it. Overall 5 feet wide, 5 feet deep and 6 feet tall, dusted with flour.

A medieval mill loft platform, about 1320: a timber platform 8 feet wide and 10 feet deep raised on four rough oak posts, its plank floor 8 feet above the ground, with a low rail along the open side, and on top a heap of brown wool blankets, a wooden cup and a stub of tallow candle in a clay dish. Total height 9 feet.
A plain medieval wooden ladder, about 1320: two rough ash rails with nine round rungs, 9 feet 6 inches long and 1 foot 6 inches wide, worn smooth, dusted with flour.
A pile of medieval grain sacks: six fat sacks of coarse undyed hemp cloth tied at the neck, stacked in two layers, 4 feet long, 3 feet deep and 2 feet 6 inches tall, dusted with flour.
A plain medieval bench, about 1320: a rough oak plank 5 feet long and 1 foot 4 inches deep on four splayed peg legs, 18 inches high, dusted with flour.

The inside wall of a medieval manor hall in Yorkshire: coursed sandstone rubble under a thin coat of limewash, warm cream, the stones about a foot across showing through, the limewash darkened slightly to gray-buff near the top by old smoke; no pattern.
The floor of a medieval manor hall looking straight down: hard beaten earth mixed with lime, brown-gray, strewn with dry green and yellow rushes and a few sprigs of herbs, scattered evenly.

The open roof of a medieval hall seen from directly below: dark smoke-blackened oak rafters about 6 inches wide set every 2 feet running in parallel, with rough gray-brown boards and pale wattle between them, no cross beams.

A medieval hall screen seen straight on, about 20 feet wide and 10 feet tall: a wall of vertical oak planks with a molded top rail, with two plain square-headed doorways, each 3 feet 6 inches wide and 7 feet tall, closed by plank doors with iron latches. Dark brown oak.

A medieval painted dorser cloth hanging on a wall behind a high table, about 16 feet wide and 7 feet tall: a heavy linen cloth hung from a rod by rings, painted in bands of deep red and green with a repeating pattern of small gold leaves and a border of white flowers.

A painted wooden heraldic shield hung on a wall, about 5 feet wide and 6 feet tall, the arms of the Ashcombe family as a guess: a silver-white field with a green chevron between three green ash leaves, the shield's edge painted dark red, the paint slightly worn.

A medieval hall window seen straight on: a two-light window with pointed heads in a chamfered sandstone frame, unglazed, closed by nothing, with oak shutters folded open against each side and a stone window seat ledge. The openings are completely transparent.

The view from a window of Ashcombe Hall, a manor house high on the Yorkshire moors, on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a muddy lane and a drystone wall, sheep on rough pasture, and the brown moor rolling away into low gray cloud, a line of wind-bent thorn trees. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A medieval hall doorway seen straight on: a pointed-arch opening about 5 feet wide and 9 feet tall in a chamfered sandstone surround, its heavy oak door folded open back against the outside wall and not seen. The whole opening is completely transparent.

The view out of the hall door of a medieval manor on the Yorkshire moors on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a muddy yard with a timber barn and a thatched byre, three laborers in brown hooded tunics cutting hedge stakes with billhooks beside a growing stack of pale stakes, a wattle fence, and the moor beyond under low gray cloud. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A medieval hall dais: a low timber platform 24 feet long, 8 feet deep and 1 foot 2 inches high, its top of wide oak boards and its front faced with plain oak planks, empty.

A medieval high table, English, about 1320: a long oak table 14 feet long, 3 feet wide and 2 feet 8 inches tall on three heavy trestles, covered with a white linen cloth hanging to the floor in front, a pewter salt cellar and two pewter cups on it.

A medieval lord's chair, English, about 1320: a carved oak chair 2 feet 9 inches wide, 2 feet 4 inches deep and 5 feet tall, with arms, a tall back with a carved pointed arch and small carved leaves, and a red wool cushion on the seat. Dark polished oak.

A medieval open central hearth, unlit: a square of flat sandstone slabs 7 feet across raised 6 inches above the floor, edged with a curb of stones, a pair of heavy iron fire dogs and a heap of split logs laid ready on gray ash, no flames.

A large medieval hunting hound lying asleep, curled on its side: a lean gray-brown wolfhound-like dog about 3 feet 6 inches long and 1 foot 6 inches high as it lies, rough coat, a plain leather collar.

A medieval hall trestle table with its bench, English, about 1320: a plank table 12 feet long, 2 feet 6 inches wide and 2 feet 7 inches tall on three trestles, with a plain plank bench 12 feet long along one side. Gray-brown oak, scrubbed, bare.

A medieval standing cupboard, English, about 1320: an oak cupboard 5 feet wide, 2 feet deep and 6 feet tall with two plank doors on black iron strap hinges and a lock plate, a shelf on top holding three pewter plates standing upright. Dark oak.

A strong medieval record room door seen straight on from the landing, closed: a door of thick oak planks 4 feet wide and 7 feet tall with a pointed top, covered with a close lattice of black iron bands and studs, three separate black iron lock plates one above another down the right side, each with its own keyhole, set in a heavy chamfered sandstone surround. No handle, no window.

A low medieval stone doorway seen straight on: a round-headed opening about 3 feet 6 inches wide and 7 feet tall in pale honey-gray ashlar with a plain chamfer, no door. The whole opening is completely transparent.

The view through a doorway down a medieval stone spiral stair: the first worn sandstone steps curving down and away to the left around a round central post, rough ashlar walls close on either side. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A strong medieval door seen straight on from inside a record room, closed: the back face of a door of thick vertical oak planks 4 feet wide and 7 feet tall with a pointed top, crossed by heavy oak ledges and black iron bands, with three black iron lock boxes one above another down the left side, set in a chamfered stone opening. No window.

A narrow medieval lancet window seen straight on: a single pointed opening about 2 feet 6 inches wide and 5 feet tall in a deep chamfered sandstone frame, glazed with small clear diamond quarries in a dark lead lattice, three iron bars across it. Every pane of glass is completely transparent.

The view from a window high above a chapter house in a Yorkshire abbey on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: the wet slate roofs of the cloister walks below and the square green garth with its round stone well, the long stone refectory beyond, and the brown moor under low gray cloud. Eye level about 20 feet above the garth.

A medieval seal cabinet, English, about 1300: an oak cabinet 3 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet deep and 3 feet 6 inches tall with six shallow drawers, the top drawer pulled half out and full of loose red, green and brown wax seal impressions, each with a little parchment slip; small iron ring pulls, dark oak.

A thick medieval abbey chronicle, about 1320: a large book about 14 by 10 inches and 5 inches thick, bound in worn dark red leather over oak boards with brass bosses and two clasps, lying open, several colored threads hanging out of its pages as markers, the pages in soft unreadable brown script.

A medieval necrology on its stand, about 1320: a tall oak reading lectern 4 feet 3 inches tall with a sloped desk 2 feet wide, holding a thick book bound in black leather lying open at a page of names in many hands and inks, in soft unreadable script, a black silk ribbon marking the place.

A medieval muniment chest, English, about 1250: an oak chest 4 feet long, 2 feet 2 inches deep and 2 feet 5 inches tall, completely banded with black iron straps in a lattice, three separate iron hasps and locks on the front, a small parchment label tacked to the lid in soft unreadable script, lid closed.
A plain medieval oak table, about 1300: a thick plank top 5 feet long and 2 feet 6 inches wide on two trestles, 2 feet 7 inches tall, gray-brown and dusty, nothing on it.

A medieval infirmary window seen straight on: a two-light window with round-headed lights in a chamfered sandstone frame, glazed with small clear diamond quarries in a dark lead lattice, oak shutters folded open at each side. Every pane of glass is completely transparent.

The view from a ground-floor window of a monastic infirmary in Yorkshire on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: a small walled herb garden of low raised beds edged with wattle, sage, rue and rosemary, a few bare fruit trees, a gravel path, the precinct wall beyond and low gray cloud. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A medieval infirmarian's wall shelves, about 6 feet wide and 4 feet tall: three plain oak shelves fixed to the wall holding glazed earthenware jars and pots in green and brown, small wooden boxes, a pestle and mortar, and bunches of dried herbs hanging from pegs under the lowest shelf. No readable labels.

A medieval bier with a body laid out, about 1327: a plain oak board 7 feet long and 2 feet 6 inches wide on two trestles, 2 feet 6 inches tall, with a body lying straight on it completely covered by a plain white linen sheet from head to foot, only the shape showing.

A medieval infirmary bed with a sleeping old monk, about 1327: a low oak bed frame 3 feet 6 inches wide, 7 feet long and 2 feet 2 inches high, a straw mattress and a heap of brown and gray wool blankets, under them the shape of a thin sleeping figure, only his tonsured white-haired head showing on a linen bolster, eyes closed.

A small medieval wall fireplace, about 1320, unlit: a plain sandstone fireplace 6 feet wide, 2 feet 6 inches deep and 8 feet tall with a sloping stone hood, a small iron cauldron on a trivet and a few logs laid on the hearth, no flames.

A small medieval infirmary table, about 1320: an oak table 4 feet long, 2 feet 2 inches wide and 2 feet 7 inches tall on square legs, with a pewter basin, a folded linen towel and a pottery jug of water on it.

The underside of a medieval bell tower roof seen straight up: massive rough oak beams about a foot wide running in parallel every 3 feet, with heavy gray oak boards above them, weathered and dry, a few old bird-droppings stains, no fixtures.

A low medieval tower door seen straight on, closed: a narrow door of vertical oak planks 3 feet 6 inches wide and 6 feet 6 inches tall with a round head, gray and weathered, two iron strap hinges on the left and a ring latch on the right, set in a rough stone opening. No window.

A medieval bell tower opening seen straight on: a tall pointed opening about 4 feet wide and 7 feet tall in a chamfered sandstone frame, fitted with sloping wooden louver boards set across it with gaps between them. The gaps between the louver boards are completely transparent.

The view from high in an abbey bell tower in a Yorkshire dale on a gray, rainy late-October day in 1327: the abbey's slate roofs and cloister far below, fields and stone walls, a swollen brown beck winding down the valley with a small watermill on it a mile off, and the brown moor rising on both sides into low gray cloud. Eye level about 60 feet above the ground.

A medieval chained book on a wall shelf: a short heavy oak shelf about 3 feet wide fixed to the wall on two brackets, holding a thick book bound in brown leather over boards, lying flat and closed with a red ribbon hanging from its pages, an iron chain running from its cover to a ring on the shelf.

A bell ringer's chalk board on a wall: a plain dark oak board about 2 feet 6 inches wide and 2 feet tall hung on a nail, with rows of short white chalk tally strokes and a few soft chalk marks, a stub of chalk on its narrow ledge.

A medieval bell frame with its great bell, English, about 1300: a massive frame of heavy squared oak beams 10 feet long, 7 feet deep and 14 feet tall, braced with diagonal timbers, holding a great bronze bell about 4 feet across hanging mouth down from a wooden headstock, with a large spoked wooden wheel about 6 feet across beside it for the rope. A low beam across the bottom of the frame is worn smooth where someone sits. The bell is dull greenish-brown bronze.
A new medieval bell rope hanging straight down: a pale, stiff hemp rope about 1 and a half inches thick and 13 feet long, with a striped red and white wool grip near its lower end, clean and unworn.

An old medieval bell rope coiled on the floor: a gray-brown, dirty hemp rope about 1 and a half inches thick in a loose round coil about 2 feet across and 7 inches high, one end frayed right through into loose strands.

A medieval painted timber ceiling seen straight up: smooth oak boards painted deep ultramarine blue, scattered evenly with small six-pointed gold stars about 3 inches across spaced about a foot apart, the paint slightly worn and the board joints showing as faint straight lines.

The inside of a 1920s steel mill building wall: old dark red-brown common brick in running bond, each brick about 8 inches long and 2 and a half inches tall, gray lime mortar crumbling out of the joints, black soot staining in soft patches, white efflorescence blooms and a few rust-orange drip streaks, unpainted and decades neglected.

Looking straight down at an old steel mill concrete floor: rough gray concrete worn smooth in places, dark old oil stains, fine hairline cracks, a thin layer of gray dust and grit, flecks of rust and a few tiny bright copper wire shavings, no joints or markings.

Looking straight up at the underside of an old industrial roof: corrugated steel roof deck with ribs about 6 inches apart running in one direction, painted gray long ago, now rusted orange-brown in streaks and blotches, soot-darkened, with small pinholes of rust, no beams, lights or skylights.

A large old steel-framed industrial window from a 1920s mill: a black-painted steel sash grid of small panes, six panes wide and five tall, the paint rusting, about a third of the panes broken out completely and the rest clouded wired glass. The broken-out panes are completely empty and transparent, and the remaining glass is completely transparent too, only slightly dirty at the edges.

The inside wall of a second-floor office in an 1890s brick commercial building on a small-town main street: old smooth horsehair plaster painted a pale warm gray, faint hairline cracks and a few patched spots, slightly aged, no marks.

Looking straight down at old narrow maple floorboards about 2 and a quarter inches wide, honey-brown varnish worn pale along the grain, small dark nail holes, a few scuffs, boards running in one direction, no rug.
Looking straight up at an 1890s pressed tin ceiling painted cream, a repeating square pattern of raised rosettes in 2-foot squares, the paint slightly yellowed and chipped at a few points.
A tall 1890s wooden baseboard, about 9 inches high, plain flat board with a rounded cap molding on top, stained dark walnut brown under old varnish, scuffed along the bottom edge.
A pressed tin cornice molding from an 1890s commercial ceiling, about 8 inches high, stepped profile with a small egg-and-dart band, painted cream to match the ceiling, slightly yellowed.
An old schoolhouse pendant light seen from directly below: a round white opal glass globe about 12 inches across on a brass holder, switched off.

A tall 1890s wooden double-hung window, painted dark green outside the white-painted inner frame, one large pane in each sash, a cream vinyl roller blind pulled up to the very top, brass sash lock in the middle. Every glass pane is completely transparent.

An old cast iron steam radiator standing against a wall, seen straight on: about 3 and a half feet wide and 2 feet tall, twelve rounded columns, painted silver long ago, the paint dull and chipped, a valve handle at the left foot.
A large plain cork board in a thin oak frame, 8 feet wide and 4 feet tall, completely empty except for a few loose pushpins in the top corners, ready for a detective's case notes.

A long white melamine board in an aluminum frame, 7 feet wide and 3 and a half feet tall, with two long horizontal strips of brown butcher paper pinned across it one above the other, each strip with a single penciled line along it and short tick marks, no writing.

An 1890s office door seen from inside: dark-stained oak with a large frosted glass upper panel and two flat panels below, a brass knob on the right, a brass mail slot in the lower rail with a hinged flap. The frosted glass is plain with no lettering.
An 1890s interior office door, closed: dark-stained oak with five horizontal flat panels, a brass knob on the left, a small brass key escutcheon below it.

The view from a second-floor office window down onto Second Street in Hollow Creek, a small former steel town in western Pennsylvania, on a rainy gray late-October morning in 2018: the wet street below, a row of two-story 1900s brick storefronts across the way with faded awnings and a closed shop, a parked 2015 sedan, a bare-limbed sidewalk maple with a few yellow leaves left, low gray sky, steep wooded hills behind the rooftops. Eye level about 16 feet above the street.

The view from a second-floor office window down onto Second Street in Hollow Creek, western Pennsylvania, on a rainy gray late-October afternoon in 2018: the wet street below, a row of two-story 1900s brick storefronts across the way with faded awnings, and parked at the far curb a black full-size 2016 pickup truck with a bar of amber roof lights switched off, its windows too dark and rain-streaked to see into, a sidewalk maple with a few yellow leaves left, low gray sky, wooded hills behind. Eye level about 16 feet above the street. No readable plate or lettering.

A 1950s oak double-pedestal office desk, 5 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet 9 inches deep and 30 inches tall, golden oak with a worn finish, three drawers in each pedestal with brass pulls, a green felt desk blotter on top, the surface otherwise clear.
A 2010s black mesh-back office swivel chair with padded armrests and a five-star base on casters, about 26 inches wide and 40 inches tall.
A plain 1950s wooden office side chair with oak arms, a slatted back and a worn brown leather seat pad, about 22 inches wide and 34 inches tall.

A 1980s drafting-style light table on a steel stand: a slanted white frosted acrylic top 3 feet wide and 2 feet deep in a gray metal frame, its top edge about 3 feet off the floor, a power switch on the side, switched off.
A 2017 silver laptop computer, open, 13 inches wide and 9 inches deep, the screen dark, sitting flat.
A 1950s brass and green glass banker's desk lamp, 15 inches tall, with a pull chain, switched off.
A 2010s black desk telephone with a built-in digital answering machine, about 9 inches wide and 7 inches deep, a small gray display and a row of buttons, a cordless handset in its cradle.
A thick tan manila file folder, closed, with a rubber band around it, about 12 inches by 9 and a half inches and an inch thick, lying flat.
A black hardcover pocket notebook with an elastic band, closed, about 6 by 8 inches, with a ballpoint pen lying across it.
A slate blue state police laboratory folder, closed, about 12 inches by 9 and a half inches, lying flat, with a white label on the front that reads exactly "LAB REPORT".
A small oak side table, 2 feet wide, 16 inches deep and 30 inches tall, with a black wire two-tier letter in-tray on top, empty.
A 1960s gray steel four-drawer filing cabinet, 15 inches wide, 28 inches deep and 52 inches tall, chrome drawer pulls and label holders, slightly dented.
A bentwood coat rack in dark walnut, 6 feet tall, six curved hooks at the top and a round base, empty.
A low 1960s wooden bookshelf, 3 feet wide, 1 foot deep and 30 inches tall, with a 2010s black drip coffee maker, two mugs and a stack of paper cups on top and a few phone books on the shelf.
Looking straight down at a wet gravel road shoulder: packed gray and tan crushed stone with small puddles, tufts of dead brown grass and a few fallen yellow and brown leaves, tire-pressed in places.

Looking through a chain-link fence into the closed East Mill of a western Pennsylvania steel works on a rainy gray late-October day in 2018: a weedy cracked concrete lot, and about sixty feet in, a dark two-story brick maintenance building with rows of broken steel-sash windows and a wide open doorway; behind it the long black corrugated sheds of the East Mill, a rusted overhead crane gantry and a soot-black brick smokestack, low heavy gray sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

Looking down a straight two-lane country road along a closed steel mill on a rainy gray late-October day in 2018: wet dark asphalt with a faded yellow center line running away into the distance, a chain-link fence and weeds along one side, wooded banks of bare and yellow-leaved trees on the other, and half a mile off, just showing over the treetops, the tall pole sign of a small gas station store, too far to read. Utility poles along the road. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

Along the fence line of a closed steel mill on a rainy late-October day in 2018: a long run of rusted chain-link fence on leaning posts with barbed wire on top, weeds and young sumac with red leaves growing through it, and beyond the fence an overgrown mill yard with a rail spur, rusted scrap and the brick side of a two-story maintenance building. Low gray sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

Across a wet two-lane country road from a steel mill gate, on a rainy gray late-October day in 2018 in western Pennsylvania: a steep wooded hillside of oaks and maples in faded orange, brown and yellow, a few small frame houses and a church steeple partway up the slope, utility wires along the road, low gray sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A closed double chain-link gate across a steel mill entrance, 16 feet wide and 8 feet tall, two swinging leaves on rusted round steel posts, a heavy chain and padlock where they meet, yellow police tape woven back and forth through the mesh, and a white metal sign wired to the left leaf that reads exactly "RIVERWORKS. A Stroud Riverfront Development. Site patrolled by Trent Protective Services." The open diamonds of the chain-link mesh are completely transparent.

A double chain-link gate across a steel mill entrance, 16 feet wide and 8 feet tall, seen straight on with both leaves swung fully open and back against the fence on either side, so the middle is an empty opening between two rusted round steel posts; a white metal sign wired to the left leaf reads exactly "RIVERWORKS. A Stroud Riverfront Development. Site patrolled by Trent Protective Services." The empty opening and the open diamonds of the mesh are completely transparent.

A 10-foot section of old chain-link fence seen straight on, 8 feet tall, galvanized mesh gone dull and rusty between two rusted round posts, a top rail, three strands of barbed wire above on slanted arms. The open diamonds of the mesh are completely transparent.

A 12-foot section of old rusted chain-link fence seen straight on, 8 feet tall with barbed wire on top, where the mesh has been cut from a post and peeled back in a curl to leave a ragged person-sized gap about 4 feet wide from the ground up. The gap and the open diamonds of the mesh are completely transparent.
A 12-foot section of galvanized steel W-beam road guardrail on three wooden posts, about 2 feet 6 inches tall, dull gray with rust spots and a dent.
A weathered wooden utility pole, about 30 feet tall and 1 foot thick, with a crossarm, glass insulators and a small transformer can near the top.
A clump of tall dead goldenrod and brown grass stalks in late October, about 3 feet across and 4 feet tall.

A 2018 police SUV in plain white with a dark blue stripe along the side, a black push bar, a light bar on the roof switched off, no readable lettering, about 16 feet 7 inches long, 6 feet 6 inches wide and 6 feet 8 inches tall.

The view out of a high broken window of an abandoned steel mill maintenance building on a rainy gray late-October day in 2018, eye level about 13 feet above the ground: the rusted corrugated walls and roofs of dead mill sheds close by, a soot-black brick smokestack, a rusted crane gantry, weeds and young birch trees with yellow leaves growing from gutters, low heavy gray sky.

Looking out through a wide open doorway of an abandoned steel mill maintenance building at ground level on a rainy gray late-October day in 2018: a weedy cracked concrete apron, a lot of gravel and puddles, and about a hundred feet off the chain-link fence and closed double gate of the mill's East Gate with yellow police tape on it, a country road and wooded autumn hills beyond. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

Looking out through a wide open doorway of an abandoned steel mill maintenance building at ground level on a gray, drizzly November day in 2018: a weedy cracked concrete apron, two white police SUVs with dark blue stripes and an unmarked gray sedan parked on the gravel, a portable generator with a cable running toward the doorway, and about a hundred feet off the mill's chain-link East Gate standing wide open, wooded hills with bare trees beyond. No readable lettering. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A wide open freight doorway in an old brick mill wall seen straight on, 8 feet wide and 10 feet tall: a rusted steel frame around the opening, the bottom track of a long-gone sliding door, and the opening itself completely empty and transparent.

A heavy 1950s steel mill workbench, 8 feet long, 3 feet deep and 34 inches tall: a thick steel plate top with a strip of angle iron along its front edge, four angle-iron legs and a low shelf, gray paint mostly worn to rust, a big cast iron machinist's vise bolted to one end with a small homemade wire-stripping jig still clamped in its jaws, and drifts of cut black and gray insulation and bright copper shavings on the floor beneath it under a coat of dust.

A 1950s steel mill tool crib cage, 12 feet long, 10 feet deep and 9 feet tall: walls of heavy galvanized diamond mesh in frames of steel angle, a mesh roof, and in the middle of the long front side a steel door 3 and a half feet wide of mesh in a heavy frame, closed, with a steel hasp and staple whose old weld bead is broken apart, a cut chain hanging from the door handle and two paper police evidence tags tied to the hasp. The open diamonds of the mesh are see-through.
Four old gray weathered wooden shipping pallets stacked flat on top of each other, each 4 feet by 3 feet 4 inches, the stack about 2 feet tall, a few broken slats.

A 1950s industrial steel mezzanine loft, 16 feet long and 12 feet deep: a deck of rusted diamond-plate steel 9 feet off the floor on four steel H-beam posts, a pipe railing 42 inches high around the open sides with a gap at one end for a ladder, gray paint flaking to rust, dust and debris on the deck edge.

A fixed steel ladder, 21 inches wide and 12 feet 6 inches tall, two flat steel side rails with round rungs a foot apart, rails curving over at the top as grab handles, rusted gray paint, standing upright.

A white corrugated plastic sign, 18 inches wide and 12 inches tall, zip-tied flat across the bottom rungs of a ladder with black plastic ties, printed in black block letters that read exactly "DO NOT ENTER, UNSAFE FLOOR, HCPD."
A 1950s floor-standing drill press, 2 feet wide, 3 feet deep and 6 feet tall, gray cast iron rusted brown, a round table and a three-spoke feed handle, no belt guard, dusty.
Three rusted 55-gallon steel drums standing together, each about 23 inches across and 34 inches tall, faded blue and black paint flaking, lids on.

A 2018 police portable LED work light on a telescoping yellow tripod, two rectangular light heads on a crossbar at the top, 7 feet tall, legs spread about 3 feet, switched off, a black power cord coiled at its foot.
Four black and yellow plastic barrier stanchions about 3 feet 3 inches tall, set in a rectangle about 10 feet by 5 feet, with yellow police tape strung between their tops on three sides.
A strip of bright yellow vinyl floor marking tape 3 inches wide and 14 feet long, laid flat and straight, with a foot-long black ruler mark every two feet.

A row of three new adjustable steel shoring posts with square base plates, painted bright yellow, each 9 feet tall, spaced 6 feet apart along a 14-foot length of new wood timber laid on the floor as a footing.

A stack of about a dozen bundles of stripped bright copper wire, each coiled bundle about a foot across, tied with wire and hung with small manila paper parts tags, piled 2 feet high behind a leaning sheet of gray weathered plywood 4 by 4 feet, a pair of rusted wire strippers on top, all under thick dust.

An old industrial pendant light seen from directly below: a deep green-enameled steel dome reflector about 18 inches across with a white inside, an empty socket in the center with no bulb, dusty, switched off.

Heavy galvanized expanded-steel diamond mesh seen straight on, each diamond about 2 inches wide and 1 inch tall, the strands dull gray with rust at their edges and spots of old gray paint, set against a flat, even dark charcoal gray background that stands for the dim shop beyond.

Looking straight up through the mesh roof of a steel tool cage: heavy galvanized diamond mesh, each diamond about 2 inches wide, dull gray and rusty, against a flat, even dark rust-brown background that stands for the mill roof far above.

The inside face of a closed steel tool crib door, 3 and a half feet wide and 7 feet tall: a frame of heavy steel angle painted gray and rusting, filled with galvanized diamond mesh, a flat steel pull handle on the left side, three heavy hinges on the right. The open diamonds of the mesh are completely transparent.

Police crime scene papers pinned flat to steel mesh with binder clips, seen straight on, a group about 4 feet wide and 3 feet tall: a measured pencil scene sketch of a small rectangular room on white graph paper in the middle, and around it four 8 by 10 color photographs of an empty concrete floor, a steel door with a hasp, wooden pallets and a steel shelf, each with a small yellow evidence marker in it. All writing on the papers is soft and unreadable. Nothing gruesome is shown.
A 1950s heavy steel shelving unit, 8 feet long, 2 feet deep and 7 feet tall, four gray steel shelves on angle-iron uprights, rust spots, completely empty and dusty.
A loose coil of stripped bare copper wire about 2 feet across and 5 inches tall, its old black insulation peeled off in long curls lying around it, all under thick gray dust.
