Faded sage-green Victorian wallpaper with a small repeating pattern of paler green laurel sprigs, each sprig about two inches long set on a three-inch half-drop grid, the paper slightly yellowed with age and softly worn.

Dark oak raised-panel wainscot from 1903: rectangular panels about 18 inches wide and 24 inches tall with beveled edges, set between plain flat stiles and rails about 4 inches wide, the varnish deep brown, a little worn and crazed with age. The pattern fills the image edge to edge and repeats on a 2-foot grid.

Old oak parquet laid in a herringbone pattern, each block about 3 inches wide and 12 inches long, honey-brown to darker brown, the wax finish worn paler along faint traffic paths, fine scratches, no rug.
A smooth old plaster ceiling painted warm cream, faintly yellowed with age, with a few fine hairline cracks, no beams, no medallion, no fixtures.

A tall 1903 dark oak baseboard about 10 inches high: a plain flat board topped by a rounded ogee cap molding, with a small quarter-round shoe at the floor, deep brown varnish with light scuffs along the bottom edge.
A dark oak chair rail about 3 inches high: a rounded bullnose center with a small bead above and below, deep brown varnish, worn smooth.
A dark oak crown molding about 6 inches high: a stepped cornice of a cove between two flat fillets with a small row of dentils along the bottom, deep brown varnish.

An early 1900s brass push-button light switch plate, a small upright rectangle of polished brass with a beveled edge and two round buttons stacked one above the other, the upper button black and the lower one mother-of-pearl white, two small brass screws.

A tall 1903 interior door of dark varnished oak with four raised panels, two tall above and two short below, in a molded oak casing, a round brass knob and a small brass keyhole escutcheon on the right side, closed.

A pair of tall 1903 dark varnished oak double doors in a molded oak casing, each leaf with three raised panels, tall above, short in the middle and square below, a round brass knob on each leaf where they meet, closed.

A 1903 Victorian fireplace surround and mantel for a country house: a dark carved oak mantel shelf on two fluted pilasters, framing a firebox lined with dark green glazed tiles and a black cast-iron grate holding a few unlit logs, a black slate hearth stone in front. Empty mantel shelf. 6 feet wide, 1 foot 6 inches deep, 4 feet 6 inches tall.

A carved Halloween jack-o'-lantern pumpkin, round and deep orange with a short curved brown stem, an elegant carved face of two triangular eyes and a wide crescent smile, a short burned-down candle stub inside, unlit. About 11 inches across and 10 inches tall.

An early 1900s brass three-arm electric ceiling pendant seen from directly below: a round brass ceiling rose, a short brass stem and three curved arms, each ending in a frosted glass tulip shade pointing down, switched off.

A tall 1903 double-hung sash window with a dark varnished oak frame and a wide oak sill, each sash divided into six panes by slim muntins, the old glass streaked with raindrops, plain cream linen curtains tied back at both sides. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

The view from a main-floor window of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a wet gravel forecourt, then a long drive curving down across dark lawns through low fog, bare and russet maples along it, and far down at the bottom the stone gatehouse with two small yellow lit windows beside an iron gate, a row of parked cars dimly visible on a gravel lot by the gatehouse. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones, no moon. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A large plain cork board in a simple dark oak frame, hung on the wall, its cork surface empty and clean, a few brass push pins and a small coil of red string tucked in the bottom corner.

A framed antique estate plan in a plain gilt frame behind glass: a hand-drawn plan of a country house and its grounds on cream paper in faded brown ink, with a compass rose and a small title cartouche reading exactly "BLACKTHORN ESTATE". All other lettering on it is soft and unreadable. The glass is clear.

A heavy Victorian oak pedestal desk from about 1900: a rectangular top inset with a dark green leather writing surface, two pedestals of three drawers each with brass bail pulls, dark honey oak, well kept, the top completely clear. 5 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet 9 inches deep, 2 feet 6 inches tall.

A Victorian oak swivel desk chair from about 1900 with a curved spindle back, rounded arms, a saddle-shaped wooden seat and a four-legged swivel base on small casters, honey oak. 2 feet wide, 2 feet deep, 3 feet tall.

A small round mahogany side table on a single turned pedestal with three splayed feet, and standing on it an old black rotary desk telephone from the 1950s with its handset in the cradle and a cloth-covered cord. Table 1 foot 8 inches across and 2 feet 4 inches tall; telephone 9 inches wide.

A closed black hardcover pocket notebook held shut with a black elastic band, a black ballpoint pen clipped to its cover, lying flat. 3 and a half inches wide, 5 and a half inches long, half an inch thick.

A closed plain manila file folder lying flat, a thin stack of typed white pages inside showing at the edge, a black pen clipped to the front, no writing on the cover. 9 and a half inches wide, 12 inches long, half an inch thick.

A closed slate-blue State Police laboratory folder lying flat, with a white label on the front that reads exactly "LAB REPORT" in plain black capitals. 9 and a half inches wide, 12 inches long, a quarter inch thick.

A closed buff State Police report folder lying flat, with a red rubber-stamp mark on the front that reads exactly "SUPPLEMENTARY" in capitals. 9 and a half inches wide, 12 inches long, a quarter inch thick.
A small Victorian mahogany tray table on four slim turned legs, with a dark wooden two-tier letter tray standing on it, the tray empty. Table 2 feet wide, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 2 feet 4 inches tall.

A Victorian upholstered armchair from about 1900: a high rounded back and rolled arms covered in worn oxblood-red velvet, short turned mahogany front legs on small brass casters, a loose seat cushion. 2 feet 8 inches wide, 2 feet 10 inches deep, 3 feet 3 inches tall.

A pair of tall Victorian pewter candlesticks, each holding a black taper candle burned down to about three inches, wax drips on the sticks, unlit. Each 3 inches across at the base and 13 inches tall including the candle; the pair stands about 10 inches apart.

Dressed pale gray limestone ashlar from 1903: smooth rectangular blocks about 12 inches tall and 24 inches long laid in running bond with thin pale mortar joints, faint natural speckle and slight weathering, a little darker in places with age.

A 1903 hall floor of polished marble squares set on the diagonal, alternating pale gray-white and dark charcoal-gray, each square about 12 inches, the polish dulled and fine scratches along the traffic paths, a few hairline cracks.

A dark oak coffered ceiling: a grid of square sunken panels about 2 feet across, each framed by plain oak beams about 5 inches wide with a small molded edge, deep brown varnish, the panel centers flat and plain.
A plain pale gray limestone plinth course about 8 inches high, a flat dressed stone band with a small chamfered top edge, faintly speckled, thin mortar joints every 24 inches.

The front entrance of a 1903 stone country house seen from inside: a heavy arched-top oak door with vertical planks, rows of black iron studs and long black iron strap hinges, a large black iron ring handle and a big iron box lock on the right side, flanked by two tall narrow side lights of plain leaded glass in an oak frame, all set in a pale limestone surround. The glass of both side lights is completely transparent.

A small modern 2018 security camera in a plain light-gray weatherproof box on a short wall bracket, its lens pointing down and out, a tiny red indicator dot beside the lens, a gray cable running up from it.

A tall round-headed opening in pale gray limestone with a plain molded stone edge, the empty archway where a wide oak staircase turns and climbs out of sight. The opening itself is completely transparent.

The view out through the side lights of the front door of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: wide wet stone front steps with carved jack-o'-lantern pumpkins on them, a gravel forecourt with puddles, a dark late-model sedan and a white small-town police cruiser with a blue stripe parked side by side at the foot of the steps with their lights off, the drive curving away downhill into fog between bare maples. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A tall Victorian oak hall coat stand with a turned central post, two tiers of curved brass hooks at the top and a round umbrella ring and drip tray at the base on four splayed feet, crowded with a dozen dark wool overcoats and raincoats, damp at the shoulders, one tweed cap. 2 feet 6 inches across, 6 feet 4 inches tall.

An English long-case clock from about 1820 in figured mahogany with a swan-neck pediment, a painted white arched dial with black Roman numerals and two hands, a long trunk door with a small glass window showing the brass pendulum. 1 foot 8 inches wide, 11 inches deep, 7 feet 6 inches tall.

The lower flight of a grand 1903 carved oak staircase: a straight run of fourteen wide oak steps with a dark red wool runner held by brass stair rods, rising to a square half-landing, with a heavy carved oak newel post at the foot topped by a round finial, a thick molded handrail and turned oak balusters along the open side and around the landing. 6 feet wide, 20 feet long including the landing, the landing floor 7 feet up, 10 feet tall at the top of the landing rail.

A carved Victorian oak hall chair with a tall shield-shaped back carved with oak leaves, a solid plank seat and turned front legs, dark varnish. 1 foot 8 inches wide, 1 foot 6 inches deep, 3 feet 8 inches tall.

A long Victorian oak hall table on turned legs with a lower shelf, and on its top a wet navy police officer's peaked uniform cap, dripping a little, beside a brass dish. Table 4 feet long, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 2 feet 8 inches tall.

A large Victorian wrought-iron hall lantern seen from directly below: a hexagonal black iron frame with six panes of clear beveled glass, a black iron bottom finial in the center and three iron chains rising to a ceiling hook, switched off.

Deep oxblood-red Victorian damask wallpaper with a tone-on-tone pattern of large stylized flowers and scrolling acanthus leaves in a slightly darker red with a faint sheen, each motif about 10 inches tall on a straight repeat, the paper a little faded and aged.

A tall 1903 double-hung sash window with a dark varnished oak frame and sill, each sash of six panes, raindrops on the glass, long heavy oxblood velvet curtains hanging open at both sides from a dark oak pole with ball finials. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

A long Victorian mahogany dining table on six heavy turned and carved legs, covered with a crisp white linen tablecloth that hangs about a foot over the edges, the top otherwise bare. 16 feet long, 4 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet 6 inches tall.

A Victorian carved mahogany dining chair with a balloon back carved with a small leaf crest, a seat upholstered in oxblood velvet with brass nailheads, turned front legs. 1 foot 8 inches wide, 1 foot 10 inches deep, 3 feet 2 inches tall.

A tall high-backed carved mahogany armchair for the head of a Victorian dining table, the back carved with a griffin crest at the top and upholstered in oxblood velvet, padded arms, turned front legs. 2 feet 2 inches wide, 2 feet deep, 4 feet 4 inches tall.

One formal dinner place setting on white linen, flat on a table: a white china dinner plate with a thin gold rim and a used soup plate on it, a folded white linen napkin, silver knives and forks on either side, a silver dessert spoon above, a crystal wine glass and water glass, and a small cream place card with a thin black border standing in a silver holder, its name soft and unreadable. About 2 feet wide and 1 foot 6 inches deep, 8 inches tall at the glasses.

The host's place setting at the head of a formal dinner table, flat on white linen: a white china plate with a thin gold rim, silver cutlery, a crystal glass of dark red claret barely touched, a crystal water glass, and a small silver hand bell with a black turned handle beside the plate, no napkin. About 2 feet wide and 1 foot 6 inches deep, 8 inches tall at the glasses.

A formal dinner place setting flat on white linen: a white china soup plate half full of orange pumpkin soup pushed a little away from the edge, silver cutlery, a crystal water glass with a faint dark red lipstick mark on its rim, and a small cream place card with a thin black border standing in a silver holder, completely blank. About 2 feet wide and 1 foot 6 inches deep, 8 inches tall at the glass.

An elegant adult Halloween table centerpiece: a low arrangement of small white and pale orange pumpkins, dark red oak leaves and black berries around three tall black taper candles in silver holders, the candles unlit and burned partway down. 2 feet long, 1 foot wide, 1 foot 8 inches tall.
A masquerade half mask of black velvet trimmed with a thin gold braid edge and two black satin ties, lying flat face up. 7 inches wide, 4 inches tall, 1 inch thick.
A crumpled white linen dinner napkin lying loosely on the floor. About 14 inches across and 3 inches high.

A long Victorian carved mahogany sideboard with three cupboard doors below and a row of drawers above with brass handles, a raised carved back with a narrow shelf, a few silver serving dishes on top. 7 feet long, 2 feet deep, 4 feet 6 inches tall including the back.

A cream card seating plan standing on a small silver easel: a neatly drawn long table outline with fourteen small boxes, six down each side and one at each end, soft unreadable handwritten names in each, the box at the foot left blank with a short penciled note beside it in soft unreadable writing. Card 11 inches wide and 8 inches tall; with the easel 10 inches tall.

A large early 1900s brass and crystal chandelier seen from directly below: a central brass column, eight curved brass arms each ending in a candle-style bulb holder with an unlit frosted bulb, strings of clear crystal drops hanging between the arms, switched off.

Full-height 1903 dark oak paneling: plain flat panels about 22 inches wide and 22 inches tall, each framed by slightly raised stiles and rails about 3 inches wide with a small molded edge, deep brown varnish with a soft age patina and fine grain, repeating on a 2-foot grid edge to edge.

A tall 1903 casement window in a dark oak frame filled with diamond-pattern leaded glass, each small diamond pane about 4 by 6 inches in thin gray lead cames, a few panes faintly tinted pale amber, raindrops on the glass, a wide oak sill. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops and the thin lead lines.

The view from a main-floor window at the back of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: the edge of a wet flagstone terrace with a stone balustrade, a sloping lawn strewn with wet leaves going down into low fog, the long dark wall of a clipped yew hedge maze and the pale shape of a glass greenhouse far off to one side, black trees beyond. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones, no moon. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A plain narrow jib door set flush in dark oak paneling, the same flat panels and stiles as the wall around it so it almost disappears, with a small round dark brass knob on the left side and a thin gap outlining the door, closed.

One section of a tall 1903 dark oak library bookcase, open-fronted with a molded cornice and plinth, seven fixed shelves full of old leather and cloth-bound books in browns, dark reds and greens with faded gilt spines, a few books leaning. 4 feet wide, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 10 feet tall.

One section of a tall 1903 dark oak library bookcase, open-fronted with a molded cornice and plinth, its seven shelves filled with long uniform runs of slim identical volumes bound in plain brown buckram, the foundation's annual accounts, each with a small soft unreadable gilt year on the spine, and a few gray archive boxes on the bottom shelf. 4 feet wide, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 10 feet tall.

A great antique floor globe from about 1910, the globe itself about 30 inches across in cream and faded sepia, blue and green, mounted in a heavy carved walnut stand with a brass meridian ring and a round walnut horizon ring held on four curved legs joined by a stretcher with a small compass in the center. 3 feet across, 4 feet tall.

A Victorian lady's writing desk in rosewood on slender turned legs, a low raised gallery of small pigeonholes across the back, a dark green leather blotter on the writing surface, a pen tray with a black fountain pen and a small cream box of heavy notepaper with its lid off. 3 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet deep, 3 feet 4 inches tall at the gallery.

A worn Victorian buttoned leather club armchair in dark oxblood-brown leather with deep rolled arms, a low back, a loose seat cushion and short bun feet, the leather creased and cracked with age. 3 feet wide, 3 feet deep, 2 feet 10 inches tall.
An early 1900s brass floor reading lamp on a round weighted base, a slim brass column and a pleated cream fabric shade, switched off. 1 foot 6 inches across, 5 feet tall.

White-painted horizontal tongue-and-groove wooden boards from about 1903, each board about 4 inches high with a thin shadowless groove between them, the old paint slightly flaking and cracked in places to show pale gray undercoat.

An old red brick wall laid in English bond, alternating rows of long stretchers and short headers, bricks about 8 by 2 and a half inches in varied soft reds and browns, pale lime mortar joints, light green moss and white bloom in a few joints, weathered.

A Victorian encaustic tile floor: a geometric pattern of 6-inch square tiles in terracotta red, buff cream and black forming repeating eight-pointed stars inside a square lattice, the glaze worn matte, a few chipped corners and faint water marks.

A Victorian conservatory glass roof seen straight up: white-painted cast-iron glazing bars in a regular grid with panes about 18 by 24 inches, the glass dark with the night sky behind it and streaked with running rain, the paint on the bars a little rusted at the joints.
A plain pale gray limestone coping sill about 4 inches high capping a brick knee wall, its top edge slightly rounded, a few small chips and lichen spots, thin mortar joints every 3 feet.

A tall section of Victorian conservatory glazing: a white-painted wooden frame divided by slim glazing bars into twelve tall rectangular panes, three across and four up, with a gently arched top rail, raindrops running down the glass. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

A Victorian glazed garden door painted white: a tall wooden door with a solid lower panel and eight glass panes above in two columns, a brass lever handle on the right side, raindrops on the glass, in a white-painted frame. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

The view out of a Victorian conservatory at the back of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a wet flagstone terrace with puddles and a low stone balustrade with urns, a gravel path leading off between clipped box hedges, a wide lawn strewn with wet maple leaves fading into fog, the dark line of a tall yew hedge maze in the distance. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

The view out of a Victorian conservatory at the side of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a flower border cut back for the autumn, wet shrubs, a stone bird bath, a lawn covered in wet fallen leaves, bare maples and dark pines in drifting fog. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A tall old kentia palm with long arching dark green fronds, a few browned at the tips, growing in a large round polished brass tub with lion-head ring handles on a short footed base. 5 feet across the fronds, 8 feet tall including the tub; the tub 2 feet across.

A Victorian white-painted wrought-iron plant stand with three tiers of curved shelves, holding a dozen potted moth orchids in white and pale pink in terracotta pots, some flowers drooping and leaves dry from lack of water. 3 feet wide, 1 foot 6 inches deep, 4 feet tall.

A Victorian white-painted wicker armchair with a high rounded fan back, curled arms and a faded green-and-cream striped seat cushion, the paint chipped. 2 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet 4 inches deep, 3 feet 8 inches tall.
A small round Victorian white-painted wicker side table with a lower shelf, a terracotta pot of trailing ivy on top. 2 feet across, 2 feet 3 inches tall.
A Victorian black wrought-iron garden bench with a scrolled fern-pattern back and arms and a slatted iron seat, a little rusted. 4 feet 6 inches wide, 1 foot 10 inches deep, 3 feet tall.

Faded deep burgundy Victorian wallpaper with a small gold trellis pattern of thin interlaced lines forming diamonds about 3 inches across, a tiny gold fleur-de-lis in the center of each diamond, the paper softly worn and slightly paler in places with age.

A worn Victorian wool carpet in a dense Turkish pattern: small interlocking medallions and stars about 6 inches across in dark red, navy blue and dull gold on a deep red ground, the pile worn thin along a faint central path.

A heavy 1903 dark varnished oak study door, two inches thick, with four raised panels, a round brass knob on the right side, seen from the corridor and closed in its molded oak casing; the casing on the right side at chest height is freshly split, a long pale splinter of raw oak torn out of the frame where the door was forced, a few wood chips on the sill. No keyhole and nothing else on this face.

A narrow plain 1903 door painted dull cream, with two flat panels and a small black iron thumb latch on the left side, the paint chipped around the latch, closed. Behind it is the steep stair to the attic.
A plain square-headed open doorway in a dark oak molded casing, no door in it, the opening itself completely transparent.

A heavy gilt-framed oil portrait of H. G. Blackthorn, a stern white man of about sixty in 1905 with a full gray mustache and side whiskers, pale gray eyes and a long face, standing in brown hunting tweeds with a shotgun broken over his arm, a dark green landscape behind him, painted in a dark, glossy Edwardian manner. A small brass plate on the bottom of the frame, its lettering soft and unreadable.

A heavy gilt-framed oil portrait of a white man of about fifty in the 1950s, Ambrose Blackthorn's father, with slicked-back graying hair, a long gentle face and pale gray eyes, in a dark gray three-piece suit and a regimental tie, seated in a leather chair against a plain brown background, painted in a formal mid-century manner. A small brass plate on the bottom of the frame, its lettering soft and unreadable.

A gilt-framed oil portrait of Ambrose Blackthorn, a white man of about sixty with thin silver hair swept back, a long, gentle, tired face with deep lines and pale gray eyes, in a dark green velvet jacket, seated against a dark green background, painted in a quiet modern traditional manner. Black crepe mourning cloth is draped over the top corners of the frame and hangs down both sides in folds, and a black crepe bow is fixed at the top center.
An early 1900s brass wall sconce: a small oval brass backplate and a single curved brass arm holding a frosted glass tulip shade pointing up, switched off.

A 1903 double-hung sash window with a dark oak frame and sill, each sash of four panes, raindrops on the glass, short cream linen curtains tied back at both sides. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

The view from a second-floor window of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: looking down over a wet slate porch roof onto dark lawns and the gravel drive curving away into fog, bare and russet maples, the low shapes of outbuildings and far off the small yellow lit windows of a gatehouse by the gate. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones, no moon. Eye level about 5 and a half feet above the floor, 18 feet above the ground.

A woman's black lace evening glove, wrist length, size small, lying flat and a little crumpled with the fingers spread, a tiny bead of dark red candle wax on one fingertip. 8 inches long, 3 inches wide, about half an inch high.

A narrow Victorian mahogany console table on four slim turned legs, with a carved Halloween jack-o'-lantern pumpkin and a small brass candlestick holding a burned-down black candle on top, unlit. Table 4 feet long, 1 foot 2 inches deep, 2 feet 8 inches tall.

An early 1900s ceiling light seen from directly below: a shallow round bowl of frosted white glass about 14 inches across with a faint etched leaf border, held up by three short brass chains to a small brass ceiling rose, switched off.

Old 1903 dark oak floorboards about 5 inches wide running in one direction, random lengths with tight butt joints and small square-headed nails, deep brown varnish dulled and finely scratched, a thin line of dust along the board edges.

The inside face of a heavy 1903 dark varnished oak study door, two inches thick, with four raised panels and a round brass knob on the left side, closed in its molded oak casing. A heavy old brass barrel bolt is mounted on the door at chest height near the left edge, its bolt shot fully out, but the brass keeper that held it is gone from the casing, leaving a raw pale wound of torn oak and two bare screw holes in the frame. No keyhole.

A 1903 double-hung sash window in a dark oak frame and sill, each sash of six panes, closed and locked with a brass catch on the meeting rail whose edges are thickly painted in with old cream paint, raindrops on the glass, heavy dark green velvet curtains open at the sides. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

The view from a second-floor study window of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a sheer drop of about thirty feet down the stone wall to a wet flagstone terrace with a stone balustrade, the glass roof of a conservatory catching the rain to one side, wide dark lawns going down into fog, the long black wall of a yew maze and a pale glass greenhouse in the distance, black trees beyond. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones, no moon. Eye level about 5 and a half feet above the floor, 30 feet above the terrace.

A narrow plain opening in a wall where a hinged bookcase section has swung away, its edges of bare old oak framing, a dark, steep, narrow wooden stair going down inside the wall just beyond, and a single strip of yellow police tape stretched diagonally across the opening, printed in black capitals that read exactly "POLICE LINE DO NOT CROSS". Everything inside the opening except the tape is completely transparent.

One section of a floor-to-ceiling 1903 dark oak study bookcase, open-fronted with a plain cornice and plinth, six shelves of old leather-bound books and tall gray and red auction catalogs, a few leaning over at one end. 3 feet 6 inches wide, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 9 feet 6 inches tall.

One section of a floor-to-ceiling 1903 dark oak study bookcase, open-fronted with a plain cornice and plinth, its six shelves filled with long dull runs of identical old bound volumes in faded brown cloth with soft unreadable gilt spines, a county agricultural society's proceedings, dusty and untouched. 3 feet 6 inches wide, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 9 feet 6 inches tall.

A broad Victorian partners' desk in dark mahogany with a tooled green leather top, drawers with brass handles on both sides, and on the leather a large green leather blotter with a single small white ruled index card lying on it, a brass inkstand and a fountain pen; a paler clean rectangle the size of a letter file on the blotter where something used to lie. 6 feet wide, 3 feet deep, 2 feet 6 inches tall.
A classic brass banker's desk lamp with a curved green glass shade over a brass stem and a round brass base with a small pull chain. 10 inches wide, 6 inches deep, 1 foot 3 inches tall.

A Victorian buttoned dark green leather desk armchair on a carved mahogany swivel base with four splayed legs on brass casters, the leather worn at the arms. 2 feet 4 inches wide, 2 feet 4 inches deep, 3 feet 6 inches tall.

A heavy cast brass bookend in the form of a seated griffin with folded wings on a square stepped base, the brass darkened with age except for a bright, clean polished patch on the griffin's back. 5 inches wide, 4 inches deep, 9 inches tall.

A plain white linen bedsheet laid over the shape of a man lying on his side on a floor, covering him completely from head to feet, the folds showing the outline of a shoulder and hip, nothing of the body visible. 6 feet long, 2 feet 6 inches wide, 1 foot 2 inches high.

A small 1950s electric mantel clock in a plain rounded walnut case with a cream dial, black numerals and two black hands, a thin brown electric cord trailing from the back. 8 inches wide, 4 inches deep, 7 inches tall.
A large old Persian rug in deep reds, navy and ivory with a central medallion and a wide patterned border, worn thin in places, lying flat. 10 feet long, 8 feet wide, half an inch thick.
A yellow plastic police evidence marker tent, a folded A-shaped card standing on the floor with a large black number 1 printed on each face. 4 inches wide, 3 inches deep, 4 inches tall.

A Victorian wingback armchair upholstered in worn dark green leather with brass nailheads, tall wings and rolled arms, short carved mahogany cabriole legs. 2 feet 10 inches wide, 2 feet 10 inches deep, 3 feet 10 inches tall.
A 1903 bedroom door painted soft cream with four raised panels, a white porcelain knob and a small brass keyhole escutcheon on the right side, in a dark oak casing, closed.

A 1903 bedroom door painted pale cream with four raised panels, each panel hand-painted long ago with faded climbing pink roses and green leaves, the paint softly worn and crackled, a white porcelain knob and a brass keyhole escutcheon on the right side, in a dark oak casing, closed.
Rough unpainted pine boards about 8 inches wide running vertically, gray-brown with age, with knots, nail holes, a few splits and a fine layer of dust, thin dark gaps between the boards.
Wide old pine attic floorboards about 10 inches wide running in one direction, gray-brown and unfinished, square-headed nails, a soft coat of gray dust with a few scuffed paths through it.

The underside of an old slate roof seen straight up: rough sawn pine rafters about 3 inches wide running in parallel 2 feet apart, with dark weathered roof boards laid across them, small slate nail tips poking through, cobwebs in a few corners.

The top of a steep, narrow attic stair seen as an opening in a board wall: a plain rough pine door frame with no door, a worn wooden handrail on one side going down out of sight. The opening itself is completely transparent.

A small round Victorian gable window about 2 and a half feet across in a thick white-painted wooden frame, divided into four panes by a cross of slim muntins, dusty glass with raindrops on it. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the dust and raindrops.

The view from a small round attic gable window of a 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: wet gray slate roof slopes and a tall stone chimney stack close by, and beyond and far below, dark lawns, the black outline of a yew maze and treetops drowned in fog. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones, no moon. Eye level about 5 feet above the attic floor, 40 feet above the ground.

A battered old tin steamer trunk from the 1940s, painted dark green and much chipped, with brass corner caps, two wooden slats across the lid, leather end handles and a brass hasp, the lid closed and unlocked. 3 feet wide, 1 foot 10 inches deep, 2 feet tall.

A long low row of plain brown cardboard file boxes with lids, stacked three high in neat columns, each with a handwritten year on a white label in soft unreadable marker, a little dusty. 8 feet long, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 3 feet tall.

A long low row of plain brown cardboard file boxes with lids, stacked three high in neat columns, each with a handwritten year on a white label in soft unreadable marker, a little dusty, with one box missing from the middle of the row, leaving an empty box-shaped gap and a clean square in the dust. 8 feet long, 1 foot 4 inches deep, 3 feet tall.

Old furniture stored under white cotton dust sheets: a tall wardrobe shape and a couple of chairs draped together, the sheets gray with dust, folds hanging to the floor. 5 feet wide, 2 feet 6 inches deep, 6 feet tall.
A single bare clear incandescent light bulb in a plain brown porcelain socket hanging on a short twisted cloth cord, seen from directly below, switched off.

An old cellar wall of rough fieldstone rubble from 1903, irregular gray and brown stones from fist size to a foot across set in thick lime mortar, all whitewashed long ago and gone patchy gray, with damp stains and a little white efflorescence.

An old cellar floor of worn gray-brown flagstones, irregular rectangles about 18 to 30 inches across with wide dark mortar joints, the surfaces smoothed and slightly hollowed by a century of feet, a thin film of dust.
A low brick barrel-vault ceiling seen straight up: old soft red bricks laid in long straight courses with pale lime mortar, whitewashed long ago and gone patchy gray, a few cobwebs.

A house electrical panel on a cellar wall, seen straight on: on the left, an old black slate fuse board about 2 feet square with rows of old porcelain fuse holders and brass terminals, mostly disused; on the right beside it, a new 2018 gray steel electrical enclosure with a big black lever handle on its right side standing in the UP position, and a white printed label on its door that reads exactly "MAIN HOUSE DISCONNECT. HOLLINS ELECTRIC 10/24/18. UP: ON. DOWN: OFF." in plain black capitals; gray conduit pipes running up from both.
A plain old cellar door of vertical pine planks painted dull cream gone gray, held by two black iron strap hinges, a black iron thumb latch on the right side, in a plain board frame, closed.
A plain 1903 four-panel pine door painted pale gray, scuffed at the bottom, a black iron knob on the right side, standing at the foot of a stair, closed. Behind it the stair goes up to the kitchen.

A heavy old outside cellar door of thick oak planks gone gray, banded with black iron straps, with a big black iron slide bolt drawn back to open, a little rain water darkening the bottom of the planks, in a rough stone frame, closed.

A long run of old brick wine bins built against a cellar wall: six arched bays of soft red brick, each bay stacked with rows of dusty dark green port bottles lying on their sides under a thick gray crust of dust and cobwebs, a small slate tag on each bay with a soft unreadable chalked year. 12 feet long, 2 feet 6 inches deep, 6 feet tall.
A tall old wooden wine rack of dark stained pine in a diamond lattice, the diamonds filled with dusty wine bottles lying on their sides, a few empty. 10 feet long, 1 foot 6 inches deep, 7 feet tall.

A short flight of four worn granite steps rising against a cellar wall, each step 4 feet wide with rough edges, the bottom two wet with blown-in rain, the top one dry and dusty. 4 feet wide, 4 feet deep, 3 feet tall at the top step.
An old oak wine barrel standing on end, with four black iron hoops, used as a tasting table, an empty wine glass and a corkscrew on its top. 2 feet across, 3 feet tall.
An old caged utility light seen from directly below: a clear glass bulb inside a round clear glass globe held in a black wire cage on a small cast-iron ceiling box, switched off.
An old service passage wall of plaster over brick, painted cream long ago and gone dingy gray, the paint flaking in patches to show soft red brick beneath, faint scuff marks and a few long cracks.
An old floor of worn red brick pavers laid flat in straight running rows, each brick about 4 by 8 inches, uneven and smoothed by wear, dusty gray mortar joints, a few cracked bricks.

An old basement ceiling seen straight up: plain wooden joists about 2 inches wide running in parallel 16 inches apart with the undersides of the floorboards between them, all painted cream long ago and gone gray, cobwebs in a few bays.
A plain flat pine baseboard about 6 inches high with a simple rounded top edge, painted cream long ago and gone gray, chipped and scuffed.

An open doorway in a plain painted board frame, no door in it, and just beyond it the bottom of a narrow, steep wooden stair going up, painted gray, with a plain wooden handrail on the wall side. The doorway opening around the stair is completely transparent.

A gray steel wall key cabinet about 16 by 20 inches with its door open, showing rows of small brass hooks with keys on numbered tags, one hook empty with a small white label under it that reads exactly "LOWER STAIR (SEALED). DO NOT ISSUE"; beside the cabinet, a ruled spiral notebook hanging from a nail on a length of white string, its cover lettering soft and unreadable.
A small printed white card sign in a clear plastic sleeve pinned to a wall, plain black type that reads exactly "Sealed doors are not to be opened during the event."
A low open doorway in an old brick wall with a heavy wooden lintel and a worn brick sill, no door in it. The opening itself is completely transparent.

The view through a low doorway into an old coal room under a 1903 house: a small low room of brick, its whitewashed walls gone gray and stained, an old brick floor swept bare, a single iron hook in the low ceiling, completely empty and still. Dim even gray tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A section of old painted tongue-and-groove paneling, narrow vertical boards about 3 inches wide, painted cream long ago and gone gray, dull and slightly chipped, running from floor to ceiling.

A section of old painted tongue-and-groove paneling, narrow vertical boards about 3 inches wide, painted cream gone gray, with a door-shaped panel set into it: the edges of the door freshly cut free of the old paint with a knife, leaving thin bright cut lines, flakes of paint on the floor below, and a small flush brass latch near the right edge, newly oiled and bright. Closed.

Bare old lime plaster on a hidden stair wall, never painted, gray-buff and uneven, with long fine cracks, a few patches where the plaster has fallen to show dark wooden lath strips, dust and old cobwebs.
Rough bare lime plaster seen straight up, gray-buff and uneven, cracked, with one patch fallen away showing the dark lath strips behind, thick old cobwebs.

The plain back of a hinged bookcase section seen from inside a hidden stair: rough dark unfinished oak boards running vertically in a heavy frame, an old iron hinge strap down the left edge, dusty, closed.
A small old iron spring catch on a wooden board, a hooked latch arm and a thumb lever, freshly oiled and bright, a faint dark smudge on the thumb lever where a thumb pressed it.

The inside face of a plain old door of vertical pine boards held by two cross battens, unpainted and gray with age, with a small flush brass latch near the left edge, newly oiled and bright, in a plain board frame, closed.

A narrow, steep hidden servants' stair from 1903: a straight flight of 22 plain wooden steps with steep risers, the treads under a thick undisturbed coat of gray dust with a single line of a man's smooth-soled shoe prints going up and coming down the middle, a plain round wooden handrail on iron brackets along one side, a small square plank landing at the top. 4 feet wide, 18 feet long, rising 21 feet.

Four worn old gray granite steps, each 4 feet wide with rough edges, the bottom step with a small dark chip out of its front edge the size of a thumbnail, an old brown stain in the joint below it, dusty. 4 feet wide, 3 feet deep, 2 feet 8 inches tall at the top step.

An old greenhouse floor of soft red bricks laid in a herringbone pattern, each brick about 4 by 8 inches, damp and mossy green in the joints, scattered with a little potting soil and a few dry leaves.

A Victorian greenhouse glass roof seen straight up: white-painted wooden glazing bars running in parallel about 20 inches apart with long overlapping glass panes between them, the glass dark with the night sky behind it and streaked with running rain, the paint peeling a little.

A section of Victorian greenhouse glazing: a white-painted wooden frame with three tall panes side by side divided by slim glazing bars, the paint peeling, raindrops running down the glass. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

A Victorian greenhouse door: a narrow white-painted wooden door with a solid lower panel and six tall glass panes above, a plain black iron latch on the right side, the paint peeling, raindrops on the glass. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

A hand-lettered sign on a piece of white card board pinned to a brick wall, written in neat black marker in two lines that read exactly "PROCESSION 12:00." and "Through the maze to the far gate and back."

The view out through greenhouse glass on a 1903 country estate in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: an old walled kitchen garden with cut-back beds and gravel paths, wet espaliered fruit trees on the brick wall, and far off across the lawn the dark mass of a big stone house with a few small yellow lit windows, low fog drifting over everything. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A bundle of about thirty round white paper procession lanterns, each hung from the end of a slim wooden pole about 6 feet long, each with a short white candle stub inside and an elegant masquerade half mask in black, gold or silver tied to the pole with ribbon, the poles leaning together upright against a bench. 6 feet wide, 3 feet deep, 7 feet tall.

A small Victorian cast-iron pot-bellied stove with a hinged front door and a little grate, standing on a square brick plinth, with a black iron flue pipe rising from its top and bending back into a wall. Plinth 2 feet 6 inches square and 8 inches tall; overall 2 feet 6 inches wide, 2 feet 6 inches deep, 6 feet tall to the top of the flue bend.
A small wooden crate of split kindling sticks with a red metal can of lamp oil standing beside it. Together 1 foot 8 inches wide, 1 foot deep, 1 foot 2 inches tall.

A long old wooden potting bench with a slatted top and a lower shelf, stacked with clay pots, seed trays, a trowel and a coil of twine, the wood weathered gray and stained with soil. 8 feet long, 2 feet 6 inches deep, 3 feet tall.
A long slatted wooden greenhouse staging bench on simple legs, lined with terracotta pots of red geraniums and small ferns. 14 feet long, 2 feet 6 inches deep, 3 feet tall including the plants.

A small lemon tree in a large square white-painted wooden Versailles planter with ball finials, glossy dark green leaves and a few yellow lemons. 3 feet 6 inches across the leaves, 7 feet tall; the planter 2 feet square.
A modern 2018 portable LED work light: a yellow and black rectangular lamp head on a telescoping black steel tripod stand with a black power cord, switched off. 2 feet across the legs, 6 feet tall.

A wet garden path of fine pale gray pea gravel seen straight down, small rounded stones about a quarter inch across with shallow puddles in a few low spots and scattered fallen yew needles and wet brown maple leaves.

Beyond an old stone boundary wall on a Berkshires country estate, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a narrow dark country lane of wet broken asphalt running left and right between overgrown verges, tall bare maples and dark pines crowding close on the far side, thick fog swallowing the lane in both directions, nobody in sight. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones, no moon. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

Inside a large old yew hedge maze on a country estate, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: rows of tall clipped black-green yew hedges about 8 feet high receding one behind another, narrow gravel paths between them turning out of sight, everything dissolving into thick fog within a few yards. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

Looking back from inside a yew hedge maze toward a big 1903 stone country house in the Berkshires, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a gravel path running away between tall black-green yew hedges, and far beyond the hedge tops, half hidden in fog, the steep gables and chimneys of the dark house with a few small yellow lit windows. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A straight section of an old clipped English yew hedge, dense dark black-green needles trimmed flat on the top and sides, wet with rain, a few thin gaps near the base showing brown stems. 8 feet long, 3 feet deep, 8 feet tall.
A straight section of an old fieldstone boundary wall of gray and brown stones laid dry with a rough flat stone coping on top, patches of moss and lichen, wet. 8 feet long, 2 feet deep, 7 feet tall.

An old black wrought-iron garden gate with vertical bars topped by spear finials and a scrolled top rail, hung between two square fieldstone piers with flat stone caps, closed, a heavy steel padlock hanging open on its hasp with its shackle freshly cut through and bright at the cut. Overall 8 feet wide, 2 feet deep, 8 feet tall; the gate leaf 4 feet wide and 6 feet tall.

An old weathered limestone garden bench, a plain thick slab seat on two carved scroll-shaped supports, patches of moss and lichen, wet with rain. 5 feet long, 1 foot 6 inches deep, 1 foot 6 inches tall.

The inside of an old fieldstone carriage house wall from 1903: rough gray and brown stones of mixed size laid in thick lime mortar, with patchy remains of old whitewash, some fresh gray cement repointing in a few joints from the renovation.

An old carriage house floor of worn red-brown brick pavers laid in straight rows, uneven and stained with old oil, with a few rough patches of newer gray concrete and a light scatter of sawdust and grit.

An old carriage house roof seen straight up: heavy dark timber beams about 10 inches wide running in parallel 6 feet apart, with rough pale roof boards laid across smaller rafters between them, cobwebs and a few old iron hooks.

A pair of tall old carriage house doors seen from inside, closed: vertical tongue-and-groove planks painted dark green long ago and faded and peeling, braced with diagonal Z battens, hung on big black iron strap hinges, with a heavy wooden drop bar resting in iron brackets across the middle, under a stone arch.

A wide stone-arched carriage house doorway seen from inside with its two tall faded green plank doors swung fully open against the walls at both sides, the arch empty between them. The opening between the doors is completely transparent.
A small old side door of vertical planks painted faded dark green, with black iron strap hinges and a black iron thumb latch on the right side, in a plain stone opening, closed.

The view out of the open doors of a 1903 stone carriage house on a Berkshires country estate, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a wet gravel stable yard, two Massachusetts State Police cruisers and a white crime scene van parked in it with their light bars off, a strip of yellow police tape tied between two posts, the dark stone wall of an outbuilding and bare trees in fog beyond. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A builder's trestle table made of a plywood sheet on two sawhorses, with a roll of large architect's construction drawings weighted open on it by a brick, a tape measure and a coffee mug, the drawings showing soft unreadable plans and section lines, a small yellow sticky note on one sheet. 6 feet long, 3 feet wide, 2 feet 9 inches tall.

An old rectangular inspection pit set into a carriage house floor, its top edge flush with the floor: walls lined with old dark red brick, five feet deep, and its floor paved with newer pale red bricks laid flat on mortar with pale fresh-looking joints, a short iron ladder fixed to one end. Top opening 4 feet wide and 8 feet long, 5 feet deep.

An old rectangular inspection pit set into a carriage house floor, its top edge flush with the floor, walls lined with old dark red brick, five feet deep, its newer brick floor broken through in the middle into a dark rough hole into a chamber below, broken bricks and rubble piled at one end, a short aluminum ladder leaning in. Top opening 4 feet wide and 8 feet long, 5 feet deep to the pit floor.

A rectangle of four portable black steel police stanchions on round bases with yellow police tape strung between their tops, the tape printed in black capitals that read exactly "POLICE LINE DO NOT CROSS". 7 feet wide, 11 feet long, 3 feet 4 inches tall.
A tower of galvanized steel builder's scaffolding two lifts high with wooden plank decks, cross braces and a short ladder, standing against a wall. 3 feet deep, 10 feet long, 12 feet tall.
A pile of building materials, stacked lumber and cement bags, covered by a blue plastic tarp tied down with rope, a few bricks holding the corners. 6 feet long, 4 feet wide, 3 feet tall.
A builder's steel wheelbarrow with a dented green tray, two wooden handles and a single black rubber tire, a little dried mortar inside, upright. 2 feet 4 inches wide, 5 feet long, 2 feet tall.

An old industrial pendant light seen from directly below: a round green enamel shade with a white enamel inside about 14 inches across, a clear bulb in the center, hanging from a short steel conduit, switched off.
Smooth old plaster painted a pale institutional sage green in a flat finish, a little scuffed and faded, a few filled nail holes and faint hairline cracks.
A worn 1980s office floor of 12-inch square vinyl tiles in speckled gray and off-white laid in a checkerboard, scuffed and dulled, a few tiles slightly lifted at the corners.

A 1980s suspended office ceiling of 2-foot square white mineral fiber acoustic tiles with a fine fissured texture, held in a thin white metal grid, a couple of tiles faintly water-stained, no fixtures.
A plain black rubber cove base about 4 inches high, a flat strip with a small curved toe at the floor, slightly scuffed.

A wide window in a thick stone gatehouse wall: a white-painted wooden frame with two side-by-side sashes of four panes each, a deep painted wooden sill, raindrops on the glass, a cheap white plastic venetian blind pulled all the way up. Every glass pane is completely transparent apart from the raindrops.

The view from the window of an estate gatehouse in the Berkshires, Massachusetts, late on a rainy Halloween night, October 31, 2018: a gravel parking lot along a low stone wall with ten guests' cars parked side by side, late-model 2010s sedans and SUVs wet with rain, nine of them nose-in and the one nearest the iron front gate, a dark gray full-size 2018 luxury sedan, backed in and facing out; the drive running up toward a big dark house on the hill in fog. Rain falling, dim even blue-gray night tones. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A plain 1980s solid wooden office door painted white, slightly scuffed, with a brushed steel lever handle and a deadbolt on the right side, a small wire-glass window in its upper half, in a white-painted frame, closed. The glass of the small window is completely transparent.
A row of three black iron coat hooks on a painted wooden board on a wall, a guard's navy blue rain jacket hanging from one hook with its hood down, a black umbrella hanging from another.

A 2018 security desk: a plain gray laminate office desk with two flat computer monitors side by side showing soft gray night camera views of a gate and a front door, a keyboard, a desk phone and a small white log printer with a curl of paper, cables tidied behind. 5 feet wide, 2 feet 6 inches deep, 4 feet tall to the top of the monitors.
A black mesh-backed office swivel chair with padded black arms on a five-star base with casters, a 2010s design. 2 feet 2 inches wide, 2 feet 2 inches deep, 3 feet 4 inches tall.

A row of three tall gray steel four-drawer filing cabinets side by side, each drawer with a chrome handle and a small label holder with a soft unreadable typed label, slightly dented. 4 feet wide, 2 feet 4 inches deep, 4 feet 4 inches tall.
A small wooden side table with a white plastic electric kettle, two stained mugs and a box of tea bags on it. 2 feet 6 inches wide, 1 foot 8 inches deep, 2 feet 6 inches tall.
A small 2010s oil-filled electric radiator space heater in white, with ribbed fins on four small casters and a dial on one end, switched off. 2 feet wide, 10 inches deep, 2 feet 2 inches tall.
A 1980s recessed fluorescent office ceiling light seen from directly below: a 2 by 4 foot white metal troffer with a ribbed clear plastic prismatic lens over two tubes, switched off.

The view from a 31st-floor office window on Sixth Avenue at West 47th Street, Manhattan, on a gray December day in 2018: the glass and stone towers of Midtown across the avenue, the canyon of Sixth Avenue far below with yellow taxis, water towers on older rooftops, a flat overcast sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, looking slightly down.

An old framed university diploma: a sheet of cream parchment with an ornate black engraved heading in Latin, a red wax seal and two signatures, soft and unreadable, under glass in a narrow dark wood frame with a gold fillet.

An old-fashioned wooden drafting board on a cast-iron base, the oak board 3 feet wide and 2 feet 3 inches tall tilted at about 30 degrees, about 3 feet 6 inches tall at its high edge, a sheet of graph paper taped to it at all four corners with a hand-drawn chart of boxes and arrows in pencil and ink, soft and unreadable, a pencil in the tray at the bottom.
A wooden drafting stool with a round oak seat and a foot ring, 30 inches tall.

A plain oak office desk, 5 feet wide, 30 inches deep and 30 inches tall, two drawers on the left and one on the right with small brass pulls, holding a green glass-shaded brass banker's lamp switched off, a leather desk blotter and a small wooden tray with a black fountain pen.
A brown leather executive desk chair with a tufted mid back and padded arms on a five-star base with casters, 2 feet 3 inches wide and 3 feet 6 inches tall.
A simple oak guest armchair with a gray-green upholstered seat and back, 2 feet wide, 2 feet deep and 2 feet 9 inches tall.

A wide run of oak bookshelves 10 feet long, 14 inches deep and 7 feet tall, five shelves packed with investment books, three matching editions of an old finance textbook and rows of bound foundation annual reports in assorted colors, the spines soft and unreadable.
A framed photograph in a simple silver frame on a stand, 8 by 10 inches: a gray-haired man and a silver-blonde woman on a small sailboat, both squinting into the sun and smiling.
A low oak file credenza, 5 feet long, 20 inches deep and 30 inches tall, with four file drawers and small brass pulls, a printer and a short stack of folders on top.
A prewar apartment wall of smooth old plaster painted a warm soft white, a velvety matte finish with gentle unevenness and a few faint hairline cracks.
Prewar oak strip flooring in narrow 2 inch boards, a warm honey brown with darker grain, polished and softly worn, fine gaps between some boards.
A smooth old plaster ceiling painted flat white, gently uneven, slightly aged.
A tall prewar baseboard, 9 inches tall, painted glossy white over many coats, with a molded ogee cap and a quarter-round shoe.
A slim prewar picture rail molding, 2 inches tall, painted glossy white, with a rounded top lip.
A prewar plaster cove crown molding, 6 inches tall, painted white, with a small bead along its lower edge.

A 1920s flush ceiling light seen from below: a round frosted white glass dish about 14 inches across held by a small brass center knob, inside a round plaster ceiling medallion with a leaf pattern, switched off.
A prewar apartment door from the inside, painted glossy white with six raised panels, a brass knob on the right side, a brass chain guard and a round peephole, in a painted white casing. No glass.

A prewar hall closet door painted glossy white with two tall raised panels and a glass knob on the left side, standing partly open: the door swung a little way inward, leaving an empty gap in the frame that is completely transparent.

The view into a small prewar hall closet: a man's charcoal wool overcoat and a woman's camel coat on wooden hangers, a black umbrella hooked on the rod, a pair of black rubber galoshes on the floor, and on the shelf above a few hat boxes and a clear empty space in a thin layer of dust the size and shape of a briefcase. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

The view from a fourth-floor apartment window on West 87th Street on the Upper West Side, Manhattan, on a gray December afternoon in 2018: the brownstone stoops and bay windows across the narrow street, bare ginkgo trees, a doorman in a dark coat hosing down the sidewalk, parked cars along the curb, a pot of white flowers on a stoop below, an overcast sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, looking slightly down.

A tall prewar double-hung apartment window painted white, one-over-one panes, brass sash locks, sheer ivory curtains hanging from a slim brass rod and pushed to each side. Every glass pane is completely transparent.
A cast-iron column radiator, 3 feet long and 2 feet tall, painted white over many coats, a small brass valve at one end.
An open prewar doorway: a glossy white painted wood casing with a molded head, the white paneled door swung back flat against the wall inside, the opening empty and completely transparent.

The view through an open doorway into a small book-lined study in a prewar apartment: a plain mahogany desk facing the door with a green leather blotter, and on the blotter a single typed page in a clear plastic sleeve squared neatly to the edge, a desk chair pushed in, shelves of books on every wall, a small window with a white blind. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, from about 8 feet away.
A black lacquered upright piano, 5 feet wide, 2 feet deep and 4 feet tall, the fallboard closed, a matching bench pushed under the keyboard.

A group of three framed photographs on easel backs: a 1986 wedding photograph of a young couple laughing in a silver frame, a photograph of a gray-haired man holding up a new brown leather briefcase with brass corners and a ribbon on its handle in a wooden frame, and a small snapshot of a beach, together about 2 feet wide and 10 inches tall.
A comfortable traditional sofa upholstered in faded deep blue linen with rolled arms, three loose seat cushions and two cream throw pillows, 7 feet long, 3 feet deep and 2 feet 9 inches tall.
A low rectangular walnut coffee table, 4 feet long, 2 feet wide and 16 inches tall, stacked with art books and a small bowl of clementines.
A worn brown leather club armchair with rolled arms and a seat cushion, 2 feet 9 inches wide, 3 feet deep and 2 feet 9 inches tall.
A large faded Oriental rug lying flat, 8 by 10 feet, rust red and indigo with an ivory border, softly worn.
A tall white-painted wooden bookcase, 4 feet wide, 12 inches deep and 7 feet tall, every shelf crammed with books of all sizes, some stacked sideways on top of the rows.
A brass floor lamp with a pleated cream fabric shade, 5 feet tall, switched off.
A sleek office wall of smooth painted drywall in cool pale gray, a fine matte finish, flawless and clean.
A wide-plank engineered white oak floor, planks about 8 inches wide in long random lengths, a pale matte natural finish with subtle grain, clean.
A smooth seamless office ceiling of painted drywall in flat bright white, clean and even.
A minimal flat office baseboard, 4 inches tall, painted the same cool pale gray as the wall, with a square top edge and a thin recessed reveal above it.
A square recessed ceiling downlight, 8 inches across, a flush white trim ring around a frosted lens, switched off.

The view south from a 27th-floor corner office on Lexington Avenue at East 52nd Street, Manhattan, on a cool gray December day in 2018: the Chrysler Building close by, its stainless steel crown of stacked arches and triangular windows, the long straight canyon of Lexington Avenue below with traffic, office towers on both sides, a pale overcast sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, looking slightly down.
A wide floor-to-ceiling office tower window: two large panes side by side in slim dark bronze aluminum frames with one narrow vertical mullion, no curtains. The glass is completely transparent.

The view west from a 27th-floor office window on Lexington Avenue at East 52nd Street, Manhattan, on a gray December day in 2018: Midtown towers stepping away toward the Hudson, and two blocks west, standing lower among them, the steep green copper mansard roof of an old grand hotel on Park Avenue, a flat overcast sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, looking down.
A framed law school diploma: cream parchment with an ornate black engraved heading, a gold foil seal and signatures, soft and unreadable, in a wide black mat and a thin black frame under glass.
A framed state bar admission certificate: cream paper with a black engraved state seal and calligraphy, soft and unreadable, in a wide black mat and a thin black frame under glass.

A framed color photograph in a thin black frame: two women in hard hats and dress coats at a ribbon cutting in front of a new school building, both smiling at the same camera, one with a sharp dark bob, one older with neat hair, holding giant scissors over a red ribbon.
A tall flush office suite door of rift-cut walnut veneer with a long vertical brushed steel pull bar on the right side, in a slim brushed steel frame. No glass.
A large framed abstract painting in a thin floating white oak frame: broad horizontal bands of slate gray, pale blue and cream.

A sleek reception counter of polished white Carrara marble with soft gray veining, 8 feet long, 2 feet deep and 3 feet 6 inches tall, its front a single smooth slab, a single white phalaenopsis orchid in a small white ceramic pot on top.

A modern white oak paralegal's desk, 5 feet wide, 30 inches deep and 29 inches tall, with a flat computer monitor, a desk phone, neat document trays and a small brushed steel desk nameplate reading exactly: J. HADDAD.
A black office task chair with a woman's camel wool coat draped over its back, 2 feet wide and 3 feet 3 inches tall.

A stack of four white corrugated cardboard evidence boxes with lift-off lids, each 15 by 12 by 10 inches, with printed labels and handwritten numbers in black marker, soft and unreadable, red tape across two lids.
A modern executive desk with a thick clear glass top, 6 feet wide and 3 feet deep, on two slim polished steel trestle legs, 30 inches tall, a thin laptop closed on it and a single pen.
A black mesh office task chair with padded arms on a five-star base with casters, 2 feet wide and 3 feet 3 inches tall.
A high-back executive desk chair upholstered in black leather on a polished aluminum five-star base, 2 feet 3 inches wide and 3 feet 9 inches tall.
A modern guest chair with a molded walnut shell and a black leather seat on slim polished steel legs, 2 feet wide and 2 feet 9 inches tall.
A long low walnut credenza with flush doors, 6 feet long, 20 inches deep and 28 inches tall, on a recessed black plinth, two small brass keyholes in the doors, closed and locked, the top bare.
A leather-bound telephone message book lying open, 11 inches wide when open, showing a page of printed message slips with a carbon copy page beneath, filled in with soft, unreadable handwriting.
A black three-ring binder lying open, 2 inches thick, the white spine label typed reading exactly: MATTER INDEX: RESTRICTED, open to a typed index page of dated entries, soft and unreadable.
A low modern sofa in charcoal wool with a slim steel base, 7 feet long, 3 feet deep and 2 feet 6 inches tall.
A low round coffee table of white marble on a black steel base, 3 feet across and 16 inches tall, a single art book on it.
An old office wall of painted drywall in a dull pale beige, a flat finish with scuffs, a few patched screw holes and faint tape marks.
A worn commercial vinyl tile floor of 12 inch squares in a mottled tan and gray, some squares lifted slightly at the edges, scuffed along walking paths.
An old suspended ceiling of 2 by 4 foot white acoustic tiles with a fissured texture in a white grid, a few tiles yellowed and two with faint brown water stains.

A hollow steel office door painted dark gray, a small square wire-glass window at eye level, a steel lever handle on the left side and a deadbolt above it, scuffed at the bottom. The glass is completely transparent.

The view through a small door window onto a narrow stair landing in an old two-story commercial building: a steep flight of rubber-treaded stairs going down, a steel handrail, beige painted walls, a bare bulb fixture switched off. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A brown hardboard clipboard hanging on a black wall hook, holding a sheet of lined paper written in square block capitals in black ink, soft and unreadable.
A black steel wall-mounted charging rack holding twelve black handheld two-way radios in a row of chargers, each charger with a small green indicator dot, the radios with short black antennas.
An old aluminum-framed double-hung window, one-over-one panes, a cheap white vinyl blind raised to the top, rain droplets on the outside of the glass. The glass is otherwise completely transparent.

The view from a second-floor window on Northern Boulevard in Long Island City, Queens, on a rainy December day in 2018: directly below, the edge of a tire shop's painted sign with soft unreadable lettering and a stack of used tires in the rain, the wet boulevard with traffic, the steel girders of an elevated subway line crossing, and beyond it across the East River the gray towers of Midtown Manhattan under low rain clouds. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, looking slightly down.
A plain wall calendar for December 2018 hanging from a nail, a large photograph of a mountain range above the grid of days, a few days marked with small handwritten notes, soft and unreadable.

A gray steel office desk, 5 feet wide, 30 inches deep and 29 inches tall, holding an open black laptop with a dark screen, two black radio chargers each with a handheld radio, a few printed pages tucked under the chargers with soft unreadable text, and a framed photograph of a squad of soldiers in desert camouflage.
A black mesh task chair with padded arms on a five-star base with casters, 2 feet wide and 3 feet 3 inches tall.
A two-drawer gray steel file cabinet, 15 inches wide, 26 inches deep and 29 inches tall, the drawers closed, a small key lock unlocked.

A stack of three black hard-shell equipment cases with latches and handles, the biggest 3 feet long, 2 feet wide and 14 inches tall, about 3 feet tall in all, a few scuffs and white stenciled numbers.
A plain black plastic stacking chair on a chrome sled base, 20 inches wide and 32 inches tall.
A small black laminate utility table, 2 feet square and 30 inches tall, holding a black drip coffee maker, a sleeve of paper cups and a can of coffee.
A plain corporate office wall of painted drywall in pale warm beige, an eggshell finish, clean and impersonal.
A commercial loop-pile carpet in plain beige with a faint darker fleck, clean and lightly worn.
A flush oak-veneer office door with a brushed steel lever handle on the right side and a door closer arm at the top, in a brushed aluminum frame. No glass.

A wall of two hundred small brass mail slots in a dark walnut frame, twenty columns and ten rows, each little brass door with a narrow slot and a tiny engraved company nameplate, the names soft and unreadable.
A 1960s office window in a brushed aluminum frame, a single wide pane over a narrow lower pane, a pale gray vertical blind drawn open at one side. The glass is completely transparent.

The view from a 19th-floor office window on Madison Avenue at East 48th Street, Manhattan, on a gray December day in 2018: buses nose to tail far below in gray slush, yellow taxis, the stone and glass office towers across the avenue, and a glimpse eastward of taller towers along Park Avenue under an overcast sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet, looking down.

An office reception desk of light oak laminate with a raised transaction ledge, 6 feet wide, 30 inches deep and 42 inches tall at the ledge, a desk phone and an open visitor log book with a pen on a chain, the writing soft and unreadable.
A long plain office counter of light oak laminate on a closed base, 10 feet long, 2 feet deep and 3 feet tall, the top bare.

A red expanding file folder lying on its side, 10 by 15 inches and 4 inches deep, its elastic cord unhooked, a row of month tabs with soft unreadable labels and a few letters on letterhead peeking out.

A slim black three-ring binder lying flat, 1 inch thick, letter size, with a white typed label on the front cover reading exactly: CARDINAL POINT TRUST: GOVERNING INSTRUMENTS, and a single side tab printed reading exactly: ARTICLE 4.

A thick gray three-ring binder lying flat, 3 inches thick, letter size, with a white typed label on the front cover reading exactly on two lines: HALVARD HOLDINGS LLC / MATERIAL AGREEMENTS, and a yellow flag tab near the front printed reading exactly: CLASS B.
A plain office visitor chair with a beige fabric seat and back on a black steel frame, 22 inches wide and 32 inches tall.
A potted ficus tree about 5 feet tall with small glossy green leaves in a plain black plastic planter, 14 inches across.
A police squad room wall of painted concrete block in pale institutional cream, the blocks 16 by 8 inches with shallow joints, a semi-gloss finish yellowed with age, scuffed and with old tape marks.
An old vinyl composition tile floor of 12 inch squares in speckled beige and gray, worn dull along the aisles, a few chipped corners.
A heavy hollow steel door painted municipal green, a narrow vertical wire-glass window at eye level, a steel push bar, a door closer arm, in a green steel frame. The glass is completely transparent.

The view through a narrow wire-glass door window into an old precinct stairwell: concrete stairs with steel nosings, a green-painted steel railing, cream block walls, a red exit sign with the word reading exactly: EXIT. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.

A wall-mounted whiteboard 8 feet wide and 4 feet tall in an aluminum frame with a marker tray. Across the top in black marker, reading exactly: 2018-018-04417. Below it a hand-drawn floor plan of a hotel mezzanine on a taped printout, a photograph of a gold wristwatch held by a magnet with a large question mark in red marker beside it, and a few lines of black handwriting, soft and unreadable.
A large cork bulletin board in an oak frame, 5 feet wide and 3 feet 6 inches tall, crowded with pinned department notices, wanted flyers and a duty roster, all soft and unreadable.

An old steel-framed police building window of wire glass, two tall panes one over the other, a fine grid of wire inside the glass, a half-raised beige vinyl blind. The glass is otherwise completely transparent.

The view from an upper window of an old Manhattan police building on a gray December day in 2018: the soot-darkened brick wall of the building next door about 20 feet away with rows of old windows, a fire escape and a rooftop water tower above, a slice of overcast sky. Eye level about 5 and a half feet.
A long cast-iron column radiator, 4 feet long and 2 feet 6 inches tall, painted cream over many coats, chipped, a valve handle at one end.

A heavy hollow steel interview room door painted municipal green, a small square wire-glass window at eye level, a steel lever handle on the left side and a steel deadbolt, in a green steel frame. The glass is completely transparent.
A wide interior observation window in a steel frame painted municipal green, one pane of clear wire glass, a half-raised beige vinyl blind at the top. The glass is otherwise completely transparent.

A gray steel detective's desk, 5 feet wide, 30 inches deep and 29 inches tall, holding three manila case folders squared to one corner, a paper takeout coffee cup with a lid, a framed photograph of two teenage girls on a boardwalk, a keyboard and a flat computer monitor with a yellow sticky note on its edge reading exactly: CALL THE ME BACK.
A gray steel office desk, 5 feet wide, 30 inches deep and 29 inches tall, holding a flat computer monitor, a keyboard, a desk phone and a few stacked folders and papers with soft unreadable text.
A worn black vinyl office chair with arms on a five-star base with casters, 2 feet wide and 3 feet 3 inches tall.
A four-drawer beige steel vertical filing cabinet, 15 inches wide, 28 inches deep and 52 inches tall, dented, drawers closed, a stack of binders on top.
A white floor-standing office water cooler with a five-gallon blue plastic bottle on top, 1 foot square and 4 feet tall, a stack of paper cones beside its taps.
A bentwood coat stand in dark wood, 6 feet tall, with a gray raincoat and a navy windbreaker hanging from its hooks.
A plain gray steel interview table bolted to the floor, 4 feet long, 30 inches wide and 30 inches tall, with a steel ring welded to its top near one edge, the top scratched and bare.
A gray steel armless chair with a molded gray plastic seat and back, 18 inches wide and 32 inches tall.
